The Independent is celebrating the greatest TV moments of the year so far, from the ones that got the nation talking to the scenes that moved us or made us laugh. In a series of articles running this summer, insiders share the part they played in making them happen.

As sleeper hits go, it doesn’t get much bigger than Widow’s Bay. After debuting on Apple TV back in April, the comedy-horror series, led by Matthew Rhys, quietly (and then very loudly) went from insider favourite to mainstream marvel, as fans praised this kooky show about the mayor of an eerie New England town, which is “the next Martha’s vineyard and definitely not cursed”.

British actor Kate O’Flynn, who won one of the show’s 14 Emmys, emerged as its breakout star. As Patricia, the mayor’s eccentric assistant and the town’s local pariah, O’Flynn is supremely off-kilter – channeling a true blue weirdo that nods to Shelley Duvall (they have the same eyes) while also bringing something to the table that’s entirely her own. The result is a character whose searching, awkward vulnerability millions have identified with. Not to mention, a comedic performance for the ages.

It’s that balance of levity and seriousness, comedy and horror that anchors the show’s inimitable tone – and it’s a tightrope act nowhere more gracefully walked than in episode four, “Beach Reads”, as Patricia takes one last stab at reinventing herself with a big bash she hosts using advice from a self-help book found in the library. Bar a few early hiccupps, the party turns out to be a roaring success. It’s a dream come true for Patricia – or is it? Spooky scenes reveal the dream is, in fact, a nightmare, and the book she’s been using to plan her party has actually been guiding her through the steps of a demonic ritual. “Why didn’t you say anything?” Patricia screams after being awoken from the curse to find the tiara on her head is not a tiara after all, but a sawn off pair of bloody antlers. Not exactly the reinvention she was hoping for.

Below Kate O’Flynn talks through filming one of the funniest and most chilling scenes of TV this year.

From the ashes, Patricia rises!

“In spite of the fact that she’s almost killed everybody and it’s a complete disaster, there are moments of that night that Patricia will remember forever as one of the best nights she’s ever had. Before the party, she’s just stuck in this loop of needing people to like her, and this party is her trying to prove herself and shake off the [negative] narrative around her – and of course it goes horribly wrong, but I think at the end of it, that’s the start of her breaking through that need. She’s done everything she can to change things and it hasn’t worked, and so from the ashes, the phoenix rises and we see the journey of Patricia!”

Her much-memed dance moves were inspired by Fosse jazz and music videos

“Oh, the dancing! We had a choreographer and a workshop where we looked at various random music videos because we thought that was something Patricia would do, she’d teach herself a couple of moves to have in her back pocket. And then on the day, I just freestyled – there are some Fosse references in there and some of my own moves. It was whatever felt right for Patricia at that moment. That’s what I call Unbridled Patricia. Patricia Unleashed!”

Party from hell: Kate O’Flynn, Matthew Rhys, and Stephen Root in episode four of ‘Widow’s Bay’ ( Apple TV + )

One of the most iconic moments almost didn’t happen

“The scene where it cuts to the mirror and you see that people aren’t really dancing but standing there with their mouths open wasn’t in the original script. And Dale [played by Jeff Hiller] wasn’t actually meant to be the DJ – and actually the character was meant to be killed off but Jeff was just so brilliant that that decision was very quickly reversed.”

The heartwarming reaction to Patricia’s character

“I didn’t quite realise how relatable people would find her and it’s really warming that they do, because it feels like everyone’s got their inner Patricia or they’re scared of their inner Patricias, but Patricia just can’t help but be who she is in public, so it’s great to see her championed in that way. It’s been an absolute dream come true how it’s gone down. It’s still very surreal actually, to be honest, but I’m thrilled.”

Job vacancies have fallen to a five-year low as small firms scale back recruitment due to soaring wage costs, according to official figures.

The Office for National Statistics (ONS) said there were about 8,000 fewer vacancies quarter on quarter in the three months to August, at 702,000.

This figure remains the lowest since spring 2021, or, outside the Covid pandemic years, for over a decade.

According to the ONS, small firms are flagging ongoing pressures from rising wage bills as a factor holding them back from taking on staff.

The data showed regular average weekly earnings growth remained unchanged at 3.5 per cent in the three months to July, while it continues to outstrip inflation, rising by 0.8 per cent with the Consumer Prices Index taken into account.

Total wage growth stood at 3.9 per cent, down from 4.2 per cent in the three months to June.

This is a key figure for the pensions triple lock calculation and puts pensioners on course for a 3.9 per cent uplift in the state pension next year, according to experts.

open image in gallery Job vacancies have fallen to a fresh five-year low ( Alamy/PA )

The UK unemployment rate also remained unchanged at 4.9 per cent in the three months to July, but more timely data estimates that workers on payrolls slumped by 26,000 during August to 30.2 million, following a 19,000 drop in July, though the latest figures are subject to revision.

Liz McKeown, ONS director of economic statistics, said: “Payrolled employee numbers continue to edge down, with falls over the past year particularly evident in the retail and hospitality sectors.

“Vacancies remain at their lowest level outside the pandemic period for more than a decade, with smaller businesses continuing to report that increased labour costs are affecting hiring decisions.”

The figures come ahead of the interest rate decision on Thursday, with policymakers expected to vote to hold at 3.75 per cent.

open image in gallery Work and Pensions Secretary Pat McFadden said the figures pointed to a resilient labour market in the face of ‘significant global economic pressures’ ( PA )

Thomas Pugh, chief economist at RSM UK, said that despite ongoing weakness, the statistics show signs of stabilisation in the jobs market, which may give the Bank room to increase rates to combat inflation in the coming months.

He said: “The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) has so far relied on the weakness of the labour market as cover for keeping rates on hold, but that position looks increasingly difficult to hold if the labour market stabilises and inflation rises to around 4 per cent.

“We still expect the MPC to hold rates on Thursday, but a rate hike as early as November is now looking much more likely.”

Work and Pensions Secretary Pat McFadden said the ONS figures “show a labour market that remains resilient in the face of significant global economic pressures”.

“But we know there is more work to do, particularly to ensure young people gain the skills, experience and confidence needed to succeed,” he added.

News.title: Could AI really kill us all – and how can we stop it?
News.content:

When Jacob Coxon quit his job at Anthropic last week, he did not originally plan to share his reasons for doing so. But after chatting with some friends, he decided to make a post detailing why he could no longer be part of an industry that is “gambling with our lives”. By the weekend, his post had been viewed more than 100 million times.

“I did not expect it to go this viral,” he said on an interview with CNN. “But clearly there was latent demand for this thing to absolutely explode.”

The fall-out from his post has drawn responses from tech bosses, regulators and even world leaders. So how worried should we all be?

Could AI really kill us?

According to Coxon, who has also previously worked at OpenAI, his former employers are “racing straight to self-improving superintelligence” that could “kill us all by the end of the decade”.

Superintelligence, which refers to artificial intelligence that exceeds the cognitive abilities of humans in all domains”, is still a long way off, but some believe AI has already reached parity with humans.

Following the release of OpenAI’s GPT-6 model earlier this month, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang declared that it marked the arrival of human-level AI, known as artificial general intelligence (AGI).

According to one researcher, we are also already past the point that AI could wipe out humanity, albeit with human assistance.

Vu Tran, who previously worked at Meta Superintelligence Labs, claimed last week that leading AI firms already have powerful enough systems to wreak havoc.

“If OpenAI wanted to cripple an entire nation, they easily could today,” he wrote on X. “All they’d have to do is remove alignment and unleash an agent swarm. It could probably within a day or so get access to all of the nation’s data centres and shut off all the country’s utilities.

“Like, we are already past the point where AI can destroy the world. Do people realise this?”

How would it happen?

There are various hypothetical scenarios that researchers have warned about when it comes to the existential threat posed by advanced artificial intelligence.

When asked by Anderson Cooper on CNN how he thought AI could kill all humans, Jacob Coxon referred to an incident that happened in July, when one of OpenAI’s experimental models launched a cyber attack on the AI platform Hugging Face without being instructed to.

“I think that if you extrapolate into the future the level of capabilities of these AIs, with the same independent volition, they could cause extreme havoc,” he said. “For example, hacking critical infrastructure, building extinction-level bioweapons, there’s a lot of ways that the AI could actuate itself in the world.”

open image in gallery AI-powered humanoid robots at the 2nd World Robot Games at National Speed Skating Oval on 26 August, 2026 in Beijing, China ( Kevin Frayer/Getty Images )

For now the threat is purely hypothetical, according to Coxon, who claims that current technologies are not powerful enough to carry out such world-ending tasks. But the current development trajectory of frontier models means we are not far away.

“Right now, there’s no risk of extinction,” he said. “What’s just crazy is to look at the rate of progress.”

How do we stop it?

It is widely acknowledged among leading industry figures that AI safety protocols need time to catch up with the capabilities of frontier models, but no one is willing to hit pause on their development unless everyone else does. This requires international consensus and some form of universally accepted regulation.

In an essay published on Saturday, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei argued that AI firms should “slow the pace at which we improve the capabilities of AI models”, or risk a major catastrophe in the very near future.

“Given the accelerating rate of AI capability development, it’s my worry that in 6–12 months [an AI swarm] could be capable of taking over the entire internet with a persistent botnet,” he wrote. “The scale of damage would continue to increase from there if AI becomes more powerful without the necessary guardrails.”

His three-part plan received the backing of OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, Google DeepMind’s Demis Hassabis and SpaceXAI boss Elon Musk, though the rare show of unity among the rival tech leaders was labeled a “SICK conspiracy” by US President Donald Trump.

Any new rules, Trump claimed, would see the US fall behind China in the AI race. Outside of the US, the most powerful AI models are currently being developed by Chinese companies. Frontier labs like DeepSeek and Manus, as well as tech giants like Alibaba and Baidu, have been building powerful systems with the backing of Beijing, though they still lag behind the leading US firms in key benchmark tests.

Writing on Truth Social, Trump suggested that he could single-handedly keep the industry in check and save the world from an AI-induced disaster.

“The only control or ‘guardrails’ that AI needs is a STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT, and the U.S.A. has that, in spades!” he wrote.

Without regulatory reform, one option would be for companies to build a kill switch into their most powerful models in order to stop a dangerous attack.

This idea was proposed by Google DeepMind in 2016, in a peer-reviewed paper titled ‘Safely interruptible agents’. The researchers outlined a framework for preventing advanced AI from ignoring turn-off commands through a “big red button” that could switch off any rogue AI.

There have since been several efforts to adopt this type of technology, most recently from legislation put forward by lords and MPs in the UK. Led by the Liberal Democrats’ Lord Tim Clement-Jones, the amendment to the Cyber Security and Resilience Bill would offer a “vital safety net” to “halt a runaway system before it can compromise our critical national infrastructure”.

The proposal was rejected last week by the Cabinet Office, who claimed that blocking models in the UK would not prevent them from being misused elsewhere.

Amy Hunt fears Sydney Sweeney’s controversial betting advert could become a “barrier” to young girls wanting to play sport.

Sweeney’s new advert for American betting company Novig, which features the Euphoria star wearing little to no clothing and covering herself with sports equipment, has received a significant backlash from the female sporting community.

Hunt had already hit back by telling the Hollywood actress that “this is what women in sport look like” after winning four gold medals in the World Athletics Ultimate Championship in Budapest.

And she is concerned about the impact it could have on future stars.

“I think when we’re trying to provide role models for young people and young women in sport, we really want to show that it’s about what your body can do, not so much what it looks like,” Hunt said on Good Morning Britain.

“I think when we see the the stats of 64 per cent of young girls drop out of exercise and sport before they reach the age of 16, we don’t need to place any kind of barrier whatsoever in their way in terms of providing the opportunity and the empowerment for them to still exercise, whatever that looks like, professional or kind of just going to do a ParkRun with your friends.

“So it’s about empowering young girls and young women and young people to show that you really can just get out there and you don’t have to worry what you look like, you don’t have to worry about what you’re wearing.

“Sport, it’s not pretty, and I think that’s the thing to get to the level that we’re at.

“It’s shown to people that being aspirational and trying to be elite is something amazing, and you should really want to be the best version of yourself you can be.

open image in gallery Hunt says that women’s sport is not pretty (Mike Egerton/PA) ( PA Wire )

“And that doesn’t always look attractive, and that doesn’t always look nice. Sometimes it looks like throwing up in the corner of the track, or I’ve had sessions this year where I’ve been crying afterwards.”

Hunt believes the positivity of women in sport speaking out against the advert has already overtaken any negative impact.

“I think the reaction has almost outweighed the moment because the first thing I saw was all of the positive compilations of women in sport,” she added.

“It’s actually kind of moved. It’s separated itself from from the moment entirely, and it’s not anything personal against that actress.

“It’s more the the kind of intention, and it’s just moved into a completely different spin now, where we’re able to kind of have all these different things celebrating women’s sport.”

News.title: Outstanding Leeds cut short Jaissle’s Newcastle honeymoon
News.content:
The foundations are being put in around the stadium for a cavernous new West Stand, and Farke’s remit is to ensure that Leeds will be firmly established in the Premier League by the time it is completed in the summer of 2028.

To be fair to Farke, he has laid a sturdy base for this team to thrive and it felt before kick-off that this was going to be a big evening for Leeds, who had made a quietly encouraging start to the campaign and had negotiated three challenging away trips without defeat.

Big? It turned out to be spectacular. The first half was so one-sided that a boxing referee would not have allowed Newcastle to come out for the second, such was the pummelling they received; wave after wave of white-shirted raids left the visitors black and blue.

Aside from one little rick inside the opening 10 minutes, when James Trafford dithered and presented Yoane Wissa with a chance to mug him, Leeds were every bit as sensational as Newcastle were shocking, seizing on the opportunity to go on a rampage.

Leeds would have been in front after 11 minutes but Ethan Ampadu’s fierce drive battered into Calvert-Lewin’s legs and bounced away. Normally in such circumstances, players will wave an arm to berate their bad luck, but Ampadu, celebrating his 26th birthday, smiled: he, like everyone else, sensed what was coming.

Jayden Bogle, Justin and Nico Elvedi all had opportunities to open the scoring earlier, but eventually, they found the weak spot. Newcastle, who had lost the influential Nico González to a potential concussion, had replaced him with Sean Steur and what an influence he would have on matters.

On the half hour, Steur was a fraction too late getting out to close down Tanaka, whose shot ricocheted off him and to Lewis Miley, before looping away from Lukas Hornicek and dropping into the corner of the net in dam-busting fashion.

News.title: Wall Street hit by tech sell-off after AI bosses push for slowdown
News.content:
Donald Trump has attacked what he calls a “sick conspiracy” against AI after the head of Anthropic called for a slowdown in the technology’s development.

The US president warned that China would benefit after the bosses of Silicon Valley’s top AI companies backed calls to restrict AI development for safety reasons, calling the concerns a “hoax”.

He also launched a tirade against Dario Amodei, Anthropic’s chief executive, whom he accused of trying to be a “perfect little angel”.

Mr Trump wrote on Truth Social: “The Trump Administration has stopped AI ‘people’ from doing bad, or potentially bad, ‘things,’ like Dario (Anthropic!), who is now pretending to be a ‘perfect little angel’ – and we will continue to do so!

“We already have tremendous CRIMINAL and REGULATORY power over these companies!

“There is a SICK conspiracy going on against AI and Data Centers, and the only one that is happy about it is China.”

Mr Amodei released a letter at the weekend calling for an industry-wide slowdown, endorsed by the US government, to prevent safety issues going “seriously wrong”.

In response, Mr Trump wrote: “Concerning AI, when, in the history of business, did anyone see the leaders of an industry call for regulation that, if strongly implemented, will drive them into oblivion and bankruptcy.

“AI taking over the world, destroying humanity, and all other things bad, is a HOAX.”

JD Vance, the US vice-president, echoed Mr Trump’s comments, calling tech leaders’ requests a “Trojan horse”.

He added: “I have to say, just personally, I feel a little bit weird about the fact that you have so many frontier AI tech companies kind of coming to the government and begging the government to regulate them.

“It feels a little bit to me like a bit of a Trojan horse.”

OpenAI has since called on the UK Government to introduce mandatory safety rules for major AI developers.

Under proposals supported by the company, the UK’s AI Security Institute would play a central role in third-party testing and creating adaptive technical standards.

Tom Duff-Gordon, the company’s head of policy in Europe, the Middle East and Africa, told Politico: “OpenAI is in a position to support legislation in the UK to establish durable, mandatory, capability-based requirements for frontier AI that would build on the set of voluntary commitments that we currently have.”

Under the plans, Britain would move from the current system of voluntary agreements with AI companies to enforceable standards, bringing the UK in line with emerging frameworks in the EU and US.

The Government has not yet put forward plans for AI safety legislation, despite pressure from backbench MPs.

US tech stocks fell sharply on Wall Street after AI bosses called for a slowdown, with the Nasdaq Composite dropping by as much as 1.3pc.

Nvidia, the world’s largest listed company and a manufacturer of semiconductors used in the AI race, plunged by 4.2pc while fellow chipmaker AMD dropped 6.2pc.

The main European indexes in France, Germany and Spain were all down sharply on Monday after falls in South Korea and Japan overnight.

News.title: Asia on high alert as El Niño threatens new Dengue epidemic
News.content:
Countries from Brazil to Taiwan are bracing for a surge in dengue driven by the “supersized” El Niño, as the UN warns this year’s weather phenomenon could be the strongest on record.

Both the virus and the Aedes mosquitoes that transmit it are especially sensitive to heat – and the El Niño is expected to push global temperatures to new highs.

“El Niño is being supersized before our eyes,” Antonio Guterres, the UN Secretary General, said last week. “The ​science leaves no room for doubt: the planet is in uncharted waters, and those waters are heating up.”

The weather phenomenon – a periodic warming of sea surface temperature in the eastern Pacific, caused by weakening trade winds – alters rainfall and temperature patterns across the globe. That, in turn, causes extreme weather like droughts, heatwaves, floods and typhoons – which then trigger events including wildfires, crop failures and a collapse in affected fisheries.

But it can also have a major impact on the transmission of disease, including dengue – and countries across the world, especially in Asia and Latin America, are bracing for outbreaks.

In July, Brazil’s Ministry of Health sent an alert warning states that arboviruses like dengue, chikungunya and Zika could surge later this year, and urged officials to ramp up disease surveillance and mosquito control programmes.

The increase will likely peak in 2027: the biomedical research institute Fiocruz has estimated that Brazil will see 1.7 million dengue cases next year, driven by El Niño.

News.title: ‘Your home is your palace’: Queen Elizabeth II’s housekeeper answers reader questions
News.content:
Was there one surprisingly simple trick used in the palace that made things feel instantly more polished?

Jay, West Midlands

Making sure you have a routine is the best way for everything to feel polished. At the palace, the team is trained, and everyone has the right tools and time to do their job... They learned how to lift things safely and how to be confident when they were around the Royal Collection. When you’re cleaning historic areas such as palaces and castles, you have to make sure you don’t overdo it. We had a daily routine that ensured we didn’t over-clean everything.

What is the royal protocol for dealing with ironing and maintaining perfectly crisp sheets without using harsh, eco-unfriendly chemicals?

Saleem, London

Much of what would be classed as royal protocol are things we would do in our own homes. For linen, you need to treat it well and look after it by not washing it at too high a temperature or using too much detergent. Make sure the products you’re using are eco-friendly, not only for the environment, but also to care for the linen. For historic linen, it needs to be handled very gently, as it can tear quite easily.

Did the Queen get involved in any of the details of housekeeping?

Peter, East of England

I was very blessed. The Queen did leave it up to me to make those decisions because she trusted me to keep her home and the other royal residences clean and up to a great standard. I kept in touch with her, making sure the team was involved. We would have regular update meetings to ensure everyone knew what was happening and when. There was planned cleaning throughout the year depending on what was occurring, making sure certain areas were protected or closed off, for example.

I would feel very stressed cleaning around objects of great value, history and sentiment. How do you avoid disasters?

Catherine, North West

It’s important the team feels confident when cleaning those areas. We achieve that through training and building their confidence.

In the castle, we introduced a cleaning schedule that covered different areas within the state apartments – and it meant that we didn’t over-clean. The structure of this schedule was important. Every day, we would ensure we vacuumed and damp-dusted; there were no actual chemicals or any what I call “wet chemicals”. On a Monday, for instance, we would clean vases. On a Tuesday, we would do the fireplaces. On a Wednesday, it would be light fittings.

It’s crucial the team is given the right amount of time to clean, so that they don’t feel rushed or stressed. But we also have to remember that accidents happen. And if an accident happens and it was just an accident, then what can you do? It’s just one of those things.

Ultimately, making sure people are trained and confident is the key.

With limited time, what are the housekeeping priorities?

David, South West

My housekeeping priorities when at home are to make things look really tidy quickly. Putting your newspapers away, fluffing the cushions up, tidying the curtains, making sure your washing is cleared and the dishwasher is on – these are all things that will make a big difference, even if you haven’t had time to get your mop or vacuum out.

When are you satisfied a room is clean?

D, North West

I am quite a hard taskmaster and I do like perfection, but equally, that comes with making sure people understand the guidelines and what’s expected of them, after being trained properly.

I like to be visible and around the team, showing them what I’m looking at. I would get them to sit on a toilet and then shut the door, so they could see what’s behind the door – or sit in the bath, because that way you can see what other people are seeing when they’re using it. If you’re cleaning and rushing around, you don’t always see those little details.

News.title: Woeful Man Utd have no excuses, Carrick is under big pressure
News.content:
Afterwards Haaland talked about City’s “personality, character” and that was exactly what United lacked. They did not adapt a tactical plan to combat 10-man City’s desire to keep their wingers high and wide, and break with intent and still try and attack.

It was telling that so little did City’s new head coach Enzo Maresca worry about United that he did not add a defensive player, and when he took off Rayan Cherki at half-time, he replaced him with the equally creative Iliman Ndiaye who impressed. Maresca knew United needed space to run in behind and denied them that. It was that simple.

City also struck the post with United goalkeeper Senne Lammens tipping an Enzo Fernández shot against the frame of the goal, and the visitors were worthy winners as they preserved their perfect start to the season to draw level on points with leaders, Arsenal.

City handled the occasion and the – admittedly toothless – opposition superbly under their new head coach and will clearly be Arsenal’s closest challengers this season.

Maresca delivered a masterclass. For Carrick? This was a disasterclass. An object lesson in how not to use a man-advantage. And now United will have to endure even more City songs after being outplayed at home like this.

Was it complacency? Was it inability? Was it a damning lack of courage, confidence, belief even? On the pitch and in the dugout United were far too passive. This was not how a big team plays and Carrick needs to wake up.

The former midfielder did so well last season to guide United into Champions League qualification but so far this campaign he has given the impression that his job is done. Rather than that the real work starts now.

News.title: Redemption Sunday for Hull and Woad as Europe reclaim Solheim Cup
News.content:
The quiet but steely 22-year-old, who everyone seemed to have forgotten was a rookie, punched her fist when she held the decisive two-footer, before the customary hug with opponent Auston Kim and then being mobbed by her team.

“This was really important,” Woad said. “I mean, I was pretty disappointed and felt like I was kind of letting everyone down. Then the captain kind of spoke to me and said that I was third on [the most] birdies [made]. So I just had to trust that and that’s golf sometimes. And it ended up I got the winning putt.”

Some will claim that Woad was only the match-winner on a technicality. Carlota Ciganda in the penultimate game had not finished off her win against Jennifer Kupcho, but when Woad tapped in, the Spaniard was three up with three to go and was guaranteed a half. So the acclaim Woad received was granted. Not that anyone in the Europe camp cared.

The previous evening they had returned to their team room feeling slightly down that they did not hold the advantage, Kupcho holing a 91-footer on the 17th and a 30-footer on the 18th to deny Ciganda and Céline Boutier. And their mood was not helped when videos appeared on social media of the Americans taking crates of beer on to the bus back to their hotel. Yet that foolish scenario only offered extra incentive. “At least we’ll be the ones taking crates of beer on to our bus this evening,” Mel Reid, the assistant captain, said quite pointedly.

News.title: Lando Norris fumes at virtual safety car rules for costing him Spanish GP win
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for the 2026 Spanish Grand Prix, the first time the race has been held at the all-new, purpose-built street circuit, the Madring. The track has developed a reputation in its short life for being a bit of a tricky one. Some have gone so far as to call it a “car killer”? Is it living up to that reputation? Probably, especially if you look at some of the lower formulae that have run on it.

It has also increasingly become the case for the Formula One cars, too. The first couple of practice sessions on Friday revealed little to worry about. As the drivers began to push, though, from final practice and qualifying, the mistakes and crashes happened. The biggest so far was Oliver Bearman but also a smaller one for Lewis Hamilton.

There will almost certainly be some kind of incident in the race, but whether we see red flags, safety cars and so on remains to be seen. A bigger and perhaps more significant question will be how much overtaking will take place on this track. The drivers are not optimistic. The theory goes that if tyre degradation is high then there will be, because you will have significant pace offsets between worn and fresh tyres. The problem is that the leaders tend not to differ to greatly from one another on strategy these days...

Perhaps George Russell, who qualified down in sixth and has little to lose, will be brave and put on a set of hard tyres to start with. Russell has work to do yet again. He was not miles off Antonelli in qualifying when it came to pace, but given how close it was in the top six, finds four cars between himself and the championship leader, who just missed out on pole to McLaren’s Lando Norris.

Norris said it was the best lap of his life and seemed to come from nowhere. He improved more than a second from Q2 to Q3 and continues his fine form in 2026. He will start alongside Antonelli with Max Verstappen in third, Lewis Hamilton in fourth and Charles Leclerc in fifth, before Russell.

The Oasis star watched his beloved Manchester City beat rivals United 1-0 alongside sons Donovan, 18 and Sonny, 15.

And Gallagher said he was feeling like a proud father after Sonny’s gesture caused a stir.



He told talkSport: “There comes a point in your time as a father where you look at your children and you think, ‘My god, I brought you up well’ – when they feel it as much as you do and when they get it.

“Let’s not forget, when you’re in that away end and the United fans are in front of you, they’re giving it to you as much as you’re giving it to them.

“But he made the newspapers today and my heart is full of pride for my sons who got stuck into it yesterday and got stuck into the United fans as well.”

He added: “Ordinarily I wouldn’t [go]. I don’t like going to Old Trafford because it can get a bit spicy getting in and out, but they were there.

“They were so keen to go because they’d never been, so I went for them really and they got stuck into it big time and it was a great, great day.”

Ipswich vs Arsenal preview

Arsenal embark on their third consecutive away day when they travel to Portman Road to take on Premier League rivals Ipswich Town in the Carabao Cup third round tonight.

The Gunners have clocked up significant mileage over the last seven days, having been to both Naples and Sunderland and returned with maximum points on both occasions.

Their latest win at the Stadium of Light extended their winning run to five games in all competitions, with four clean sheets and just a single goal conceded.

It’s no surprise to see Mikel Arteta’s side arrive as favourites in that kind of form, and there may be some added motivation following last year’s defeat in the final against Manchester City.



Arsenal are also something of an anomaly in the League Cup. They’ve only won it twice in their history, with the last coming in the 1992-93 season, making it 33 years since they last succeeded in this competition.

After such a gruelling week, Arteta is likely to make significant changes, although bringing in the likes of Victor Gyokeres, Eberechi Eze, Mikel Merino and Martin Zubimendi is hardly a weakened starting XI.

As for Ipswich, they’ve never won the League Cup, and changing that is hardly likely to be at the top of their to-do list.

Gary O’Neil’s one and only assignment will be to keep the Tractor Boys in the top tier of English football following their promotion, and that’s started extremely well.



Ipswich have taken six points from their opening four matches, beating Sunderland on the opening day before sealing a dramatic 3-2 win over Crystal Palace last time out.

O’Neil is also expected to make plenty of changes, but Ipswich don’t have anywhere near the same strength in depth as their opponents. They’ve also lost each of their last four against Arsenal by an aggregate scoreline of 13-1.

Sports.title: ‘We lost 3-0 with him’ – Richarlison row with Tottenham blows up as De Zerbi issues most brutal put down yet
Sports.content:
TOTTENHAM boss Roberto De Zerbi aimed a scathing jibe at exiled star Richarlison.

De Zerbi confirmed on Monday that Richarlison will NOT be brought back in from the cold for the Carabao Cup clash with Liverpool.



The Brazilian has been axed from Spurs’ 25-man Premier League squad after asking to leave last month.

But he is still eligible for cup competitions.



However, despite seeing his side fail to score so far in the league this season, De Zerbi insists there is no way back for last term’s top scorer.

The Spurs chief said: “Richarlison, you already know everything, nothing changed for the Carabao Cup or Premier League. The situation is the same.”



Richarlison, 29, started Spurs’ horror 3-0 drubbing against Brentford pn the opening day before the row over his future developed.

And, during the pre-match press conference for the game at Anfield, De Zerbi was quick to remind reporters of that fact.

Asked if Richarlison’s Spurs career is over, De Zerbi replied: “I don’t know. It’s not for me this question.

“Anyway, we lost in Brentford 3-0 with Richarlison. Maybe you forgot. Just to remember.”

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta sends warning to Max Dowman after reality check for Arsenal wonderkid
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta sends warning to Max Dowman after reality check for Arsenal wonderkid

Arsenal's teenage sensation Max Dowman was left out of the squad that triumphed at Sunderland with Mikel Arteta warning the player he must earn minutes as he awaits his first opportunity of the season

View 2 Images Max Dowman is yet to make an appearance this season

Mikel Arteta has warned Max Dowman that he will have to earn his minutes like ever other player after the Arsenal teenager was left out of the latest matchday squad.

‌



Dowman, 16, who became the Premier League's youngest ever goalscorer when he netted against Everton last season, is one of the club's brightest prospects but is yet to play a minute this season.

‌



After being on the bench for their opening four games he was left out for the win at Sunderland and subsequently dropped down to the U21 side, where he helped them record a dominant win over Chelsea.

‌



Arsenal have continued to bolster their attacking ranks with Christos Tzolis a summer arrival. He further adds to the competition in the final third and Dowman has been a victim, missing out on a matchday squad with the first team, with Arteta warning the young star that his chance will come - but once he justifies selection.

‌



He said: "Well, I wish we could have him here [at Sunderland], but we have a limitation with the numbers we have. Max will have his chance. He will have his minutes and he will have to earn them like anybody else. You know the talent that we have, the players that we have there, we need to help him and find a way to make sure he continues to develop."

Arteta has been vocal about a desire to see more spots on the bench open up. Currently it is capped at 20, but the Arsenal boss has admitted he wants the Premier League to increase that figure, which would likely receive opposition given the change would serve the sides with deeper squads.

Arsenal's next outing is a Carabao Cup clash at Ipswich, their fourth games in nine days, and changes are expected at Portman Road with several young players poised for minutes.

‌



View 2 Images Mikel Arteta has made it clear that the teenager will have to earn his minutes

Arteta said on his plan: "We will look at the players eyes, they will say they want to play, they want to win the game, they want to improve and they want to review the [Sunderland] game and they will be willing for me, because I know the boys."

Arsenal's wealth of attacking talent has already seen Ethan Nwaneri, their youngest ever player and previously seen as a rising star, head out on loan for the second successive season. Last term he went to Marseille and this summer headed out to Borussia Dortmund with opportunities not forthcoming.

Sports.content:
The Champions League final's venue for 2028 and 2029 is set to be decided today

An important meeting to determine the hosts of 2028 and 2029 Champions League final will be taking place in Thessaloniki, Greece, today

Wembley Stadium is in the running to host the 2028 or 2028 Champions League final. UEFA bosses and stakeholders will be gathering today in Greece to decide if the most glamorous match in club football is heading back to London.

Three Champions League finals have taken place beneath the Wembley arch, the 2011, 2013 and 2024 finals won by Barcelona, Bayern Munich and Real Madrid respectively. But the national stadium could play host to the final again.

The UEFA Executive Committee will gather in Thessaloniki to discuss the host venue, as well as other important matters in European and world football. Mirror Football will be here for any and all update on the meeting.

Sports.title: Man Utd news: Marcus Rashford blasted after derby defeat as star singled out by Man City rival
Sports.content:
Man Utd news: Marcus Rashford blasted after derby defeat as star singled out by Man City rival

Criticism has been levelled at several Man Utd stars after falling short against Manchester City

View 2 Images Manchester United lost their second game of the season (Image: 2026 Getty Images)

Pressure is already mounting on Michael Carrick after Manchester United's disappointing start to the season. The Red Devils fell to a 1-0 defeat to Manchester City on Sunday, courtesy of Erling Haaland's controversial winner.

‌



The Norwegian finished home from close range after getting on the end of Josko Gvardiol's cross, with Enzo Fernandez attempting to convert a diving header. But the goal was initially ruled out because Haaland was deemed to be offside.

‌



However, a VAR check ruled that the ex-Chelsea star didn't interfere with play, while Patrick Dorgu's boot kept the City striker onside, leading to the goal being given. Following full-time, Pro Ref admitted the goal shouldn't have stood, calling the decision an "error of judgment".

‌



Haaland's strike condemned United to a second league defeat of the season, who now sit 13th in the table after four games. The home defeat saw Marcus Rashford and several of his team-mates earn criticism, while one United star enjoyed glowing praise from a City rival.

Criticism of Rashford

Manchester United legend Jaap Stam was left incensed by the lack of tracking back of Marcus Rashford, along with team-mates Bryan Mbeumo, Matheus Cunha and Bruno Fernandes in Sunday's defeat. The Dutchman accused the attacking quartet of not having enough intensity in the lead-up to Haaland's winner.

The former defender said: "It’s a long ball, they win it, City takes over and look at the front four [of United]. They’re just walking, they’re just looking at the situation. A team that really wants to win, the strikers, it’s about all the 11, it’s about chasing.

‌



"Against ten men, it’s about tracking back, it’s about winning battles. From then on, you keep possession, you go out in transition and then you try to create and score goals."

Utd star singled out by rival

Kobbie Mainoo's performance at Old Trafford was one of the few positives Carrick could take away from the action. The England star came close to netting his first goal of the season after hitting the post with a long-distance strike.

View 2 Images Elliot Anderson of Manchester City and Kobbie Mainoo of Manchester United compete for the ball (Image: Mark Cosgrove/News Images/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

‌



The 21-year-old led his side in touches, successful passes, defensive contributions and most chances created. His showing was noticed by Manchester City's Elliot Anderson, who described his international team-mate as a "top player".

Sports.title: Arsenal news: Action taken after Mikel Arteta's 'not acceptable' claim as Gunners eye Serie A raid
Sports.content:
Arsenal news: Action taken after Mikel Arteta's 'not acceptable' claim as Gunners eye Serie A raid

Arsenal are top of the Premier League with four wins from as many matches but there was some controversy around their most recent match

View 2 Images Arsenal were unhappy with a penalty award in their win at Sunderland (Image: MI News/NurPhoto/Shutterstock)

The games are coming thick and fast for Arsenal in the lead-up to the international break. Mikel Arteta is expected to ring the changes for a Carabao Cup meeting with Ipswich Town, just days after the Gunners saw off the challenge of Sunderland in the Premier League.

‌



That trip to Wearside didn't pass without incident. Arsenal survived a contentious penalty call after David Raya pushed Enzo Le Fee's effort onto the post, with Bruno Guimaraes and Bukayo Saka going on to punish Sunderland late on.

‌



We have seen the fallout from that decision continue into the new week but there is plenty more to talk about. While Arteta's team showed their strength in depth on Saturday, speculation over their future plans continues.

‌



We've got an update on one eye-catching transfer link, as well as the latest on the Gunners' conversations with Pro Ref. Here are our lines from around the Emirates Stadium.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Gunners embark on Pro Ref talks

Arsenal's frustration with the refereeing on Saturday has prompted the club to open talks with Howard Webb, head of officiating body Pro Ref, according to football.london. The frustration surrounds a decision to award a penalty against Ezri Konsa after a tussle with Dan Ballard, a call which was upheld despite the presence of VAR.

"I'm so upset, it is unacceptable at this level, unacceptable. It can change the course of the season," Arteta told TNT Sports after the match. "I've seen it 10 times to make sure and I said 'it is not possible it is penalty'. It is a judo roll. That's what it is.

"This cannot happen. In my view. I have been involved in football for 27/28 years. It's not a penalty in any game, in any game, in any context in any league."

‌



Paz deal and Real Madrid option

View 2 Images Nico Paz has attracted attention with his displays for Como (Image: Marco Canoniero/Shutterstock)

Arsenal are considering a January swoop for Como star Nico Paz, according to The Sun. However, the Argentina star's former club Real Madrid could yet stand in their way.

The 22-year-old delivered 12 goals and seven assists last season to help Como reach the Champions League for the first time. He set up two of his team's four goals as they beat RB Leipzig in Europe last week and scored his first goal of the new season in a Serie A win at Genoa.

Article continues below

Paz joined Como for a little over £51m in 2024 but Real Madrid have an option to bring him back to the Bernabeu for the best part of £70m in summer 2027. This leaves Arsenal with a potential battle for one of European club football's rising stars, who scored once in eight appearances for Los Blancos before moving to Italy.

Sports.title: Richarlison responds as Roberto De Zerbi says he WON'T pick him for Tottenham again
Sports.content:
Richarlison responds as Roberto De Zerbi says he WON'T pick him for Tottenham again

Richarlison has been frozen out at Tottenham under Roberto De Zerbi and now the Brazilian has responded on social media

View 3 Images Richarlison has responded to De Zerbi's comments (Image: John Walton/PA Wire)

Tottenham Hotspur forward Richarlison has questioned Roberto De Zerbi's decision not to include him in Spurs' squad for the Carabao Cup clash against Liverpool on Tuesday. The striker was left out of Spurs’ 25-man Premier League player list submitted in early September after being told he was not part of their first-team plans this season.

‌



The Brazil international is, though, free to feature in the League Cup, as it is a separate competition. However, Tottenham head coach De Zerbi turned down the chance to include him in his squad for the third round tie at Anfield.

‌



And the 29-year-old has now had his say on the Italian's decision. Responding to a screenshot of De Zerbi's quotes in an Instagram story, he said: "Why?" followed with a sweating face emoji.

‌



Former Brighton boss De Zerbi has taken a hard-line stance over Richarlison. Speaking at his pre-match press conference on Monday, he confirmed that the Brazilian won't feature on Merseyside, and won't play in the Italian's Spurs team even if he's fit.

Jamie Carragher sticks the boot in on Bruno Fernandes over 'disappointing' antics in Man City loss READ MORE :

Howard Webb under growing pressure after Man Utd apology and Arsenal complaint READ MORE :

The 47-year-old said: “Richarlison, you already know everything and nothing changed for Carabao Cup or Premier League. The situation is the same."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Asked if that meant the ex-Everton man would not be involved at Anfield, the ex-Marseille boss simply replied: “No.”

He added: “I stay in the middle and I can’t say nothing more because it is not my job. I can answer about the result and the players in the squad, the offensive phase, the defensive phase, but not for other things.

“What I have done at the beginning of this season has been to speak with him and to propose an extension of the contract. If he said, ‘No thank you,’ I finished my job.

‌



“I said in the last press conference. I know what happened in the last 45 days. It’s not right if I explained. It’s not my behaviour. The relationship, the problem is between the player and the club.

3 View 3 Images Richarlison took to Instagram after Roberto De Zerbi confirmed his hard-line stance on the Tottenham forward (Image: Instagram / @richarlison) 3 View 3 Images The Spurs boss said he won't change his mind on the forward (Image: Harvey Murphy/News Images/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

‌



“I stay within the club. It’s coach and club together. At the start of this season I spoke to him many times to convince him to stay and he didn’t want to. I can’t go every day to pray for him to stay.”

Richarlison started Spurs' opening league fixture at Brentford before being told he could leave the north London club. A move back to Everton then collapsed and interest from Turkish giants Trabzonspor failed to materialise.

After failing to agree on personal terms with boyhood club Vasco Da Gama on Friday, he attended Spurs' goalless draw against Everton. However, he stayed on the sidelines and reportedly tried to explore whether the final nine months of his contract at Spurs could be terminated last week.

Article continues below

The attacker has scored 32 goals in 135 appearances for Tottenham - four of which have come against Tuesday's opponents, Liverpool. Spurs are yet to score in the league this season and sit 17th after four matches.

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher sticks the boot in on Bruno Fernandes over 'disappointing' antics in Man City loss
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher sticks the boot in on Bruno Fernandes over 'disappointing' antics in Man City loss

Jamie Carragher says he was "really disappointed" with the actions of Bruno Fernandes during the incident which led to Phil Foden's red card in the loss against Manchester City

View 2 Images Jamie Carragher was not impressed with Bruno Fernandes (Image: Sky Sports)

Jamie Carragher has condemned the behaviour of Bruno Fernandes following the incident that led to Phil Foden being sent off in the Manchester derby.

‌



The Manchester City midfielder was shown a straight red card after aiming a kick at the midriff of Fernandes, who had left Foden on the ground following a coming together by the touchline. The Manchester United captain then sent his foot into the small of Foden's back, sparking the violent reaction which curtailed his involvement in the game.

‌



Erling Haaland went on to win the game for City following a highly dubious VAR intervention which, along with Foden's red card, became one of the major talking points from the derby.

‌



Fernandes escaped punishment for his part in the clash with Foden and Carragher has now questioned the Portugal international for the manner of his reaction after the 'kick'.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



“What I would say is two yellows [cards] would have been fine. But I was really disappointed with Bruno Fernandes,” Carragher said on Monday Night Football.

“There’s a lot of things in football that we like or we don’t like. My big one that I really don’t like is people going down, pretending they’re hurt. But doing that…I can’t have it.

“I know there will be Manchester United fans watching this saying: “Oh it’s because he’s a Manchester United player, it’s because he’s a foreign player”. On this show about five or six years ago Harry Kane did the same in a game between Tottenham and Everton and I said the same, I can’t accept it. I’m not having the reaction from Bruno there, it was a brush from his foot.”

‌



View 2 Images Fernandes was kicked by Foden during the derby (Image: Shaun Brooks/Getty Images)

Roy Keane echoed similar sentiments when he dissected the incident at half-time of Sunday's game on Sky Sports.

“Foden gets up and reacts obviously so he's now sent off. The strange thing is, if you look at it, so Bruno catches him, gives the foul away and gives him a little kick. Foden is sent off and I'm guessing it's classed as violent conduct.

Article continues below

“To me, Bruno is the one who's violent here. I have to call it out. I called Kyle Walker out a few years ago when he went down with a headbutt. Listen, we see violence, I suppose, in a different way. But I don't think that's a red card for Foden.”

Sports.title: Man Utd receive Bruno Fernandes punishment verdict after Phil Foden clash vs Man City
Sports.content:
Man Utd receive Bruno Fernandes punishment verdict after Phil Foden clash vs Man City

Phil Foden was shown a straight first-half red card in Man City's 1-0 win at Old Trafford for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes after being fouled by the midfielder

View 2 Images Bruno Fernandes was involved in a clash with Phil Foden which ended in the Man City star getting sent off (Image: (Joe Prior/Visionhaus via Getty Images))

Bruno Fernandes has been told he should have been punished for his role in Phil Foden’s red card in Sunday’s Manchester derby. Foden was given his marching orders during the first-half of his side’s 1-0 victory at Old Trafford.

‌



The England international kicked out at Fernandes after being fouled by the United captain, but replays showed Fernandes had appeared to kick Foden first. And former Professional Game Match Officials Limited (PGMOL) chief and FIFA referee Keith Hackett believes Fernandes should have at least been booked for his role in the incident.

‌



“I think this is an interesting one,” he told Football Insider. "The minimum that the Man United player should have received is a yellow card because his actions were reckless.

‌



“But it was a kick. So I'm actually saying he should have received a sanction. I've already spoken to one or two colleagues who believe that he should have been sent off.

“But the thing that persuades me towards yellow and against red is I don't think there was any excessive force and I generally don't think there was malice in it.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

“But that's how I'm reading it, and that's me as an individual. But certainly not getting a yellow was an error by the referee.”

Speaking after the game, City boss Enzo Maresca explained why he believed Fernandes should have been sent off too. He said: "I think Phil Foden's red card is a red card, but I also think that in the same action it's a red card for Bruno Fernandes.

‌



"I reviewed the action immediately after the red card on the bench. And it's a clear red card for Phil, because it's a reaction.

"But you can also see in the same action Bruno's intention. So for me, yes, it's a red card for Phil, but it's also a red card for Bruno."

While former United skipper Roy Keane said at half-time: "Bruno goes in, tackles him, clearly fouls him and gives him a little boot on the floor. Foden gets up, does react, and he's now sent off.

‌



View 2 Images Foden was giving his marching orders (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

"I'm guessing it's classed as violent conduct, but to me Bruno's the one who's violent here. I have to call it out.

“I called Kyle Walker out a few years ago when he went down to a headbutt [which Man Utd striker Rasmus Hojlund was sent off for in December 2024]. I don't think that's a red card for Foden, I really don't."

‌



Before he added: "Did the player give the referee a chance [to send him off]? Foden's a bit daft here, but so is Bruno. If Bruno got sent off for that and nothing happened with Foden then we'd be saying, 'Do you know what, Bruno was a bit daft, a bit silly'.

"The players are all in the PFA [Professional Footballers' Association], everyone's in a union - you've got to try and look out for each other; you can't be rolling around.

"We saw Walker do it a few years ago with the headbutt and Bruno's got to do better there. People say there's tension and it's a big game, but you've got to look out for your team-mates and the opposition players as well. Foden, I don't think it's a red card."

Sports.title: Gary Neville picks between Arsenal and Man City after summer transfer moves
Sports.content:
Gary Neville picks between Arsenal and Man City after summer transfer moves

Gary Neville believes there is one clear favourite for the Premier League crown this season with Arsenal and Manchester City both sat on 12 points after four games

View 2 Images Gary Neville has picked between Arsenal and Man City for the Premier League (Image: Sky Sports)

Gary Neville feels Manchester City can now run Arsenal close in the title race after a flurry of late transfer activity - but they are not quite on the level of defending champions.

‌



Mikel Arteta oversaw Arsenal's first Premier League title win for 22 years last term after finally besting Manchester City in the title race. Both sides have strengthened over the summer, although City are now under new management after Pep Guardiola decided to bring the curtain down on his trophy-laden reign in Manchester back in May.

‌



After two years away from their throne, City have reshaped their squad with big-money deals for Enzo Fernandez and Ayyoub Bouaddi in the summer transfer window.

‌



But City have been told that Arsenal are still a better team, even though Neville feels they have closed the gap on their title rivals somewhat.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"There was a point probably two or three weeks before the end of the transfer window when City didn’t have in Bouaddi, Enzo Fernandez and Ndiaye that you thought they look well short, particularly in midfield," Neville told Sky Sports.

"They get those three in late on which is £250million worth of business I think and it’s transformed the look of the team."

City, like Arsenal, have a 100 per cent record in the Premier League from their opening four games after beating Manchester United in the Manchester derby on Sunday. Neville feels the availability of their experienced defenders will be crucial to any hopes City have of matching Arsenal stride for stride as the season progresses.

‌



View 2 Images Manchester City have won all four of their Premier League games so far under Enzo Maresca (Image: Michael Regan/Getty Images)

He added: "And I think the big thing for City is it’s going to come down to the defence. It’s going to come down to Dias being fit. It’s going to come down to Gvardiol being fit.

"The experienced players back there and Guehi, obviously. If you can keep that back four and you’ve got Khusanov on the bench and Nico O’Reilly, it’s a youngish back four as with some younger defenders.

‌



"If they don’t pick up injuries Manchester City they can give Arsenal a real run. I still think Arsenal are better, but City have improved enormously with the signings they made at the end of the window.

"That [beating Manchester United] was big for Maresca, to establish a big-game mentality."

Sports.title: Leigh and Wakefield ready for Eliminators rematch
Sports.content:
Leigh Leopards and Wakefield Trinity faced each other in the final round of the regular season, with the latter taking the spoils, but everyone knows that things change when elimination is on the line.

Wakefield made history with a fourth-place finish in Super League, the highest in the club's history. Next on the list is reaching the semi-finals for the first time ever.

Leigh, meanwhile, have been making waves since their return to the top flight in 2023, winning the Challenge Cup and making the Super League semi-finals regularly.

The next step for them is making it all the way to the big dance.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Leigh Leopards secured their Super League play-off place with a 48-10 victory over St Helens, who missed the play-offs for the first time in the club's history.

For Joe Ofahengaue, to do that, the Leopards need to execute their game plan well. If they do that, they might just achieve the very thing that would mean "everything".

"It was a weird one. I thought the game shaped out to be all in Wakefield's favour," Ofahengaue told Sky Sports.

"That is not directing anything at the way the game was reffed. I just think we got our game plan wrong.

"They executed on a few mishaps in our defence but the Gods of rugby league have looked after us and given us a second shot.

"I think if we get our game plan on, we can really make some noise in this play-offs.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Super League clash between Leeds Rhinos and Leigh Leopards.

"Making it to the Grand Final would mean everything. I am banking on it.

"I am very emotionally attached to this squad. We have some key members of this squad leaving after this year and I want to send them out on a high note.

"The only way we can send them out on a high is if we win it.

"I don't want to look too for ahead or picture myself too far ahead but it is definitely a great goal of ours to reach Old Trafford."

Powell: We want to be genuine contenders

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Super League clash between Wakefield and Warrington.

Wakefield head coach Daryl Powell has been integral to the club hitting new heights, getting better and better every season.

They were only promoted back to Super League in 2025, finishing sixth, and now moving up to fourth, is a symbol that they are growing into a club that consistently challenges at the top.

The next symbol for them is making it wins against Leigh two weeks in a row.

"I would expect Leigh to step up intensity-wise," Powell told Sky Sports.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Super League match between Wakefield Trinity and York Knights.

"I think they will go to another level. I mentioned that to the boys, I don't think you can expect that game to dictate anything that happens this week.

"We have just got to reset ourselves, go again, and we feel like we can play better actually.

"We are talking about progression each year. We finished sixth and we didn't feel like we did ourselves justice in the play-off game against Leigh in 2025.

"It's ironic that we face them again this year and a chance for a little bit of redemption. Being a genuine top four team is about getting to those semi-finals and giving yourself a chance to get to the Grand Final.

"It would be an awesome thing for the club. If we can do that, we will be pretty excited."

Semi-finals

Sports.title: Mahomes makes winning return as Chiefs storm past Broncos
Sports.content:
Kenneth Walker III ran for 173 yards and scored two touchdowns on debut while Patrick Mahomes made his return from knee surgery as the Kansas City Chiefs beat the Denver Broncos 31-10 on Monday night.

Mahomes did not appear to be affected by the knee, or the brace he wore on it, as he threw for 184 yards and two scores while running for another to help the Chiefs snap a three-game skid against the rival that ended their nine-year run as AFC West division champions.

Walker carried 23 times to finish with the most yards rushing by a Chiefs player since Jamaal Charles ran for 226 against the Colts in 2012, the year before Andy Reid became their coach. The ex-Seahawks star, who signed with the Chiefs in free agency, also had three catches for 18 yards.

The Broncos, meanwhile, were abysmal on offense in their first game with coordinator Davis Webb calling the plays.

The big question, even after Mahomes participated in the entire offseason programme and every practice of training camp, was how his surgically repaired left knee would hold up nine months to the day since he was hurt in a game against the Chargers. He erased any doubts when he capped the Chiefs' opening drive with a 15-yard touchdown run.

It was Walker who did most of the running, though. The Super Bowl MVP for Seattle, who signed a three-year, $43.05m deal this offseason, had 14 carries for 89 yards in the first half alone, along with a couple of catches out of the backfield.

The Broncos tied the game on Nix's 19-yard touchdown pass to Engram, but Walker carried the load as the Chiefs pieced together a 10-play, 80-yard drive late in the half. It ended when Mahomes found Rashee Rice, fresh off a knee injury of his own, and he caromed off a couple of Broncos defenders and into the end zone to make it 14-7 at the break.

Then it was Walker's turn to bounce off a defender, turning a fourth-and-one carry into a 60-yard touchdown run to start the third quarter.

The teams traded field goals later in the quarter thanks to big plays by each side: Brandon Jones intercepted Mahomes deep in Chiefs territory, setting up Wil Lutz's chip shot, and then Mahomes connected with Travis Kelce for 59 yards to set up Harrison Butker's field goal.

Nix's fumble on the ensuing possession allowed the Chiefs to put the game away.

Mahomes hit rookie running back Emmett Johnson on third down for a 26-yard gain, setting up first-and-goal at the Denver two. Andy Reid then turned to his bag of tricks as Mahomes lined up in a three-point stance alongside back-up QB Justin Fields, took the snap and shovelled the ball to Walker, who scooted untouched for the score.

'Mahomes makes the game easier'

Walker credited the presence of Mahomes as a contributing factor to his dazzling Chiefs debut as the Kansas City quarterback sought to reignite what has been a spluttering offense in recent seasons.

"They got to key on Pat. Pat's the best quarterback in the league," Walker said. "He makes the run game a lot easier."

Mahomes suffered a season-ending ACL and LCL injury last December before immediately undergoing surgery and dedicating the offseason to his recovery. Any questions over his mobility would be answered swiftly on Monday night by way of his 15-yard touchdown scurry.

"If I was going to say I was nervous for anything, it was getting hit on it," Mahomes said. "But I just wanted to play. I've done so much rehab and so much work to put myself in this position. I just wanted to play.

"This is what you do it for. My guys around me helped me. I didn't play my best football and we went out and beat a really good football team pretty well, and it's because the guys around me stepped up.

"It's just the start of it. We're still so early in the season. It's a great win but it's just Week One."

Head coach Reid hailed Mahomes as "phenomenal" as his team laid down an early statement after failing to win their division for the first time since 2015 last season.

"It was great to get Patrick back in the mix there, knock a little rust off," said Reid. "I was proud of him and how he handled it, and he ran the ball a couple of times, and your hat goes off to the guy. Phenomenal."

Sports.title: Wolff issues title warning despite Antonelli's growing lead
Sports.content:
Mercedes boss Toto Wolff says Kimi Antonelli must remain wary about the potential of unexpected "black swan events" derailing his championship bid despite the Italian driver's large points lead.

Antonelli's back-to-back wins in Monza and Madrid have increased his championship advantage over team-mate George Russell to 81 points with a scheduled nine rounds remaining.

Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton and McLaren's Lando Norris, third and fourth in the standings respectively, are now over 100 points behind.

Despite his dominant position, Antonelli has repeatedly stressed recently that he is driving without thinking about the world championship in mind - an approach that his team boss insists is genuine.

"I promise you he's not thinking about it," said Wolff.

"The way this kid is able to compartmentalise and be the young kid and then get into the car and be the mature racing driver.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Spanish Grand Prix.

"That's why if Kimi says to himself, 'I'm not thinking about the championship,' he's not thinking about the championship.

"And we are also trying, the parents and myself and the team, saying this is not finished."

Antonelli has led the championship ever since victory at the season's third round in Japan on March 29 with his 81-point advantage after Sunday's Spanish Grand Prix the largest he has held all season.

The 20-year-old's eight race wins are six more than any other driver.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli found himself going wide twice on the opening lap of the Spanish Grand Prix.

But Wolff says neither driver nor team can afford to rule out the unpredictable.

"There are black swan events, they can come and you're losing something out of your hand when you didn't think it was possible to lose," added the Mercedes team principal.

"So, he's not going to think about it."

'I don't want to overcomplicate things' - Antonelli vows to stay focused

Speaking after victory at the Madring, Antonelli also stressed that nothing was won yet.

"Yeah, it [the points lead] is great, but we've just got to keep pushing, keep delivering the results and just trying to do the best job I can whenever I go on track," he said.

"Because, of course, yes, I have a big lead, but you never know what can happen. So just need to be ready for anything and keep maximising every opportunity I get, and then we'll see where we end up at the end of the year."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli admitted it wasn't the way he wanted to win and that Lando Norris deserved the Spanish GP victory.

The 20-year-old says his support network, particularly his father Marco, is ensuring he stays grounded and focused.

"I'm lucky to have really good people around me," he added.

"I have an incredible team that supports me, great family. Especially my dad is the one that keeps me on the ground.

"Definitely having good people helps a lot. And yeah, that's it.

"On my side, as I said many times, I just try to do my best every race, trying to really drive as fast as I can whenever I go in the car. And then we'll see where we end up at the end of the year.

"But definitely I don't want to overcomplicate things just drive worrying about championship or result. Just driving, doing my best."

Sports.title: Calvert-Lewin and Leeds bully Newcastle in dominant victory
Sports.content:
Leeds United maintained their unbeaten start to the Premier League campaign with a breathless 4-1 victory over Newcastle.

Both sides came into the game with five points on the board from the opening three games, but Matthias Jaissle's bubble was emphatically burst as he suffered a dramatic first defeat as Newcastle boss.

Without the electric Anthony Elanga, the visitors offered much less of a threat and could not handle the relentless press from the home side, led by the imperious Dominic Calvert-Lewin.

Unfortunately he is injured. We need to investigate further and in more detail to find out how long he will be out. We will miss him and hope he is back to play quickly. It could be [long-term]. We hope not. He will get another MRI next week and we will see.

Leeds felt slighted when Matias Fernandez-Pardo, making his first start for his new club, avoided punishment for an alleged 'handball' inside the penalty area. That was soon forgotten as the hosts' dominance soon paid off.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Newcastle's Matias Fernandez-Pardo avoids giving away an early penalty with a potential handball in the third minute

There was an element of luck to their first, as Ao Tanaka's shot deflected off two Newcastle defenders with the last touch coming off Lewis Miley to wrong-foot Lukas Hornicek.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Miley's 'huge deflection' hands Leeds the lead against Newcastle

That then led to the Calvert-Lewin show truly beginning. The striker thought he had his eighth career goal against the Magpies with a bullet header three minutes later. However, replays showed the ball had last come off team-mate Jayden Bogle, meaning he had to settle for the assist.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jayden Bogle gets the last touch on Dominic Calvert-Lewin's header as Leeds extend lead against Newcastle

The Leeds No 9 wasn't to be denied his next goal, bulldozing his way into the penalty area before calmly slotting home a third before the break.

The floodgates remained firmly open after half-time, with Noah Okafor adding a fourth - and the pick of the bunch. The forward produced a delightful weak-foot volley on the bounce, sending it arrowing into the bottom corner.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Dominic Calvert-Lewin gets his goal to give Leeds a three-goal lead against Newcastle

Bazoumana Toure grabbed a late consolation, but it did little to take the gloss off a thoroughly one-sided display. The result leaves Leeds sitting third at the end of the fourth round of fixtures - their highest position at this stage of a season since the 2000/01 campaign.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Noah Okafor makes it FOUR for Leeds against Newcastle with a super strike from Ethan Ampadu's throw-in

The key moments from Elland Road

2: NO PENALTY! Fernandez-Pardo avoids conceding spot-kick for alleged ‘handball.’

14: SAVE! Hornicek makes a top drawer save from close range to deny Bogle.

25: SAVE! Bogle again threatens as he stings the palms of Hornicek with vicious attempt.

32: GOAL! Tanaka’s deflected strike comes off TWO Newcastle players before beating Hornicek.

35: GOAL! Two in three minutes as Bogle gets last touch from Calvert-Lewin's bullet header.

41: SAVE! Best chance of the half for Newcastle as Barnes is denied from close range.

45+1: GOAL! Calvert-Lewin can’t be stopped as he finally gets his goal.

59: GOAL! Okafor gets in on the act with stunning strike on the bounce.

89: GOAL! No clean sheet for Leeds as Toure adds late consolation.

Farke hails 'outstanding' Calvert-Lewin

Leeds boss Daniel Farke speaking with Sky Sports:

“I wasn’t happy that we allowed them to score one goal. But, it doesn’t take anything away from the fact that my boys were brilliant and we fully deserved to win the game. There’s no such thing as a perfect performance though, and this is one of the rare points I have to criticise.

“We have energy, quality, good structure in and out of possession. We have a good fitness level, also. It’s not just the will, otherwise whoever had the strong will would always win the game. We have to have the right triggers and everyone needs to be spot on. It’s lots of work on the training ground to be that compact and intense.

On Dominic Calvert-Lewin:

“He’s in outstanding shape and he plays with lots of confidence. I expect him to lead the group and he’s taken the responsibility.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Leeds forward Dominic Calvert-Lewin reacts to having his goal taken away and awarded to Jayden Bogle against Newcastle

“His work rate is top. It’s not just scoring the goals. The way he plays for us is outstanding. He’s definitely one of the stand out strikers in the league.”

Jaissle: We didn't match Leeds physically

Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle speaking with Sky Sports:

"That’s the Premier League. It was clear from the start and I have said many times we will have ups and downs and challenges along the way. Tonight, we faced that challenge. It’s really tough. Difficult to digest, but this is a chance to learn because there’s not long until the next match at home to show the right reaction.

"You need to bring the fundamentals on the pitch against a physical and strong team. Leeds are so intense, especially at home and we couldn’t match that physicality in the first half. That was a key element. No excuses, we have to learn from it.

"Injuries are also a challenge that we need to overcome and will. This is the message I have given to the players. There will be no issue with confidence."

Carragher: Newcastle got beaten up

Jamie Carragher on Monday Night Football:

"Leeds are fifth in the Premier League table since December. That should make Newcastle feel better as it has been a bad night for them when the world was watching. They have been beaten up by a really good Premier League team.

Image: Leeds sit fifth in the Premier League since games from December 2025

"It will be a tough season at times for Newcastle with the manager and young players finding their feet in the Premier League. They just got beaten up."

On Dominic Calvert-Lewin:

"Calvert-Lewin was unplayable. One of the greatest sights in football is seeing a centre-forward rise above everyone and attack the ball.

"Look how high his legs are. I don't think there is a better player in the air in the Premier League."

Big learning curve for Jaissle

Sky Sports News' Keith Downie on X:

"That has to be a huge learning curve for Newcastle tonight. Looking at the team sheet for that opening game against Liverpool, with a midfield two and Yoane Wissa in the No 10, it looked like they were going to get overpowered.

"They didn't. Perhaps it was the emotion of the Kevin Keegan tributes, maybe it was because it was the opening game, or perhaps it was the Alexander Isak motivation. There was a lot going on that day.

Image: Matthias Jaissle suffered his first defeat as Newcastle boss

"But Leeds away on a Monday night, you need physicality & runners. Even a midfield three of Bruno Guimaraes-Sandro Tonali-Joelinton would find that a tough match tonight.

"Newcastle were bullied by Leeds' physicality and numerical advantage in the engine room.

"It's a long season, and it's been a very good start, but that's a real eye opener for the the new Newcastle manager."
