Sports.title: Bayern Munich tipped to go after struggling Premier League striker as future Harry Kane replacement
Sports.content:
Bayern Munich tipped to go after struggling Premier League striker as future Harry Kane replacement

Bayern Munich have been tipped to target Nick Woltemade as Harry Kane's surprise successor.

Kane is still banging in the goals for the time being, becoming the fastest player to 100 goals for Bayern, but at 33 the Ballon d'Or contender is heading towards the back end of his career.

2 Kane opened his Bundesliga account for the season with the winner for Bayern against Elversberg on Sunday Credit: Getty

And European football expert Andy Brassell reckons the German giants will eventually sign Woltemade, despite the striker's struggles at Newcastle.

Germany international Woltemade joined Newcastle from Stuttgart last summer, just before Alexander Isak left for Liverpool, and scored eight Premier League goals in his first season with the Magpies.

However, he found net just twice between the turn of the year and the end of the campaign and has since been loaned out to Juventus.

Bayern 'convinced' Woltemade would join before

Still only 24, Woltemade is theoretically yet to hit his prime years, and Brassell believes he'll make his way back to the Bundesliga with Bayern one day.

"I still think Woltemade will end up at Bayern at some point," he told talkSPORT's Hawksbee and Jacobs.

"They were convinced he would go there before Newcastle and he's had a difficult start at Juventus as well... quite a messy situation.

"They're trying to reform the front part of their team and they've ended up with this front pairing of him and Randal Kolo Muani.

"They were really out of nick in the back end of last season. It's the blind guiding the blind.

"So it is difficult as they're two good players who are trying to recover form.

"I think Bayern will be looking at that and thinking, 'We could get this guy we really wanted for maybe pennies on the pound at some point in the future."

2 Woltemade has featured in Juventus' last two Serie A games Credit: Getty

Woltemade still waiting to get off the mark for Juve

Woltemade's two appearances for Juventus so far have been as a substitute, and he's played just 44 minutes in total.

He's only managed to muster three shots in that time, all of them off target.

His loan departure came after he had made two appearances for Newcastle early in the season.

He played the entirety of the Carabao Cup second round win over West Brom before coming off the bench to set up Yoane Wissa's goal in the 2-0 Premier League victory at Tottenham.

Nonetheless, he was loaned out to Juve on deadline day.

He'll hope to get off the mark for the Bianconeri when they host Dutch side NEC Nijmegen in their Europa League opener on Thursday.

Sports.title: ‘A total mess’ – LaLiga club due to move into 70,000 World Cup stadium could be relegated after sacking manager
Sports.content:
‘A total mess’ – LaLiga club due to move into 70,000 World Cup stadium could be relegated after sacking manager

Valencia are in disarray and must avoid LaLiga relegation ahead of the move to their new stadium.

That's according to European football journalists Kevin Hatchard and Andy Brassell as they sit winless at the bottom of Spain's top flight.



3 Valencia are at risk of being relegated with their dismal start to the season Credit: Getty

After their 1-0 defeat to Sevilla on Friday night, Valencia have just one point to show for their efforts with five matches played in LaLiga.

Carlos Corberan, formerly in charge of Championship side West Brom, has been sacked as head coach of his boyhood club amid their poor run.

Ex-Chelsea chief Ron Gourlay has also been dismissed from his role as CEO of Football at Valencia, who were crowned Spanish champions in the 2003/04 season.



They are now on a treacherous path towards what would be a shock relegation just months before moving into their new stadium.

Valencia will leave their iconic Mestalla for the 70,000-capacity Nou Mestalla, which is set to cost £275million at completion and one of Spain's proposed venues for the 2030 World Cup.



However, Ches Blanquinegros have been warned that they cannot afford to be relegated to LaLiga 2 before their relocation.

Valencia were 'unforgivably terrible' at Sevilla

On Trans Europe Express, Hatchard said: "We started this with Mestalla, and the reason is it's a total mess at the Mestalla...



"Corberan, for a Valencia coach, has lasted a while, actually. He saved them from the drop in his first season, they improved upon that last season. But the truth is, this goes way beyond coaching...

"You invest nothing, what do you expect?" Brassell interjected, before Hatchard added: "This is about Peter Lim (owner), really, this is about the ownership, as it has been for a long, long time."

Brassell agreed and explained: "When you look at the fact that they're due to move into their new Mestalla, their new stadium that's been 20 years in the making, at the start of next season, they really need to be in the top flight for that.

3 Corberan was dismissed having been appointed in December 2024 Credit: Getty



"We're talking about a 70,000 stadium that's obviously going to have a part in the next World Cup. It's been through various different incarnations, abandonments, restructures.

"For ages, the facade and the foundations were just sitting there for people to look at, it was like a monument of folly, really. Whereas, now they're really close to doing it, they have to have a team that's worthwhile playing in it. 70,000 seats to fill is a lot.

"You go back to last week when they were playing against Barcelona... talking of Rodri, he's had a week where he's very much had his tail between his legs, because he got caught on TV saying to a couple of his Barcelona teammates, 'These lot are absolute rubbish'.

"Which is fine, obviously people say that sort of stuff to their teammates. Normally in the dressing room, or normally at the training ground, not in a stadium that's got 36 cameras in it and loads of other people taking social videos, and all the rest of it.



"Lip reading is the second Spanish national sport after watching football, it's very much a Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday sort of thing, so he basically had to apologise for it.

"One of the last things that Corberan did as Valencia coach was say, 'I don't accept your apology', basically. Of course, he should have been apologising himself for the performance that they gave at Sevilla on Friday night.

3 Valencia's new stadium could welcome a second-tier team next season Credit: Getty

"Sevilla are in an even bigger financial hole than Valencia - they made Sevilla look like France '98, they were absolutely, unforgivably terrible.



"I feel sorry for Corberan, but the last couple of performances have been dreadful. Even with the disquiet at the club and, as you say, it's nothing new, the performances have got to be better than that.

"I don't think they've got one of the worst three squads in the division, but Lim is going to have to put his hand in his pocket at some point."

Valencia drew 0-0 with Celta Vigo in their season opener before 1-0 and 3-1 defeats to Real Betis and Deportivo de A Coruna respectively.

A 5-0 thumping by Barcelona preceded the loss away at Sevilla, with Alaves and Real Sociedad up next before the international break.

Sports.title: Noel Gallagher has never been prouder than about what sons did to angry Man United fans
Sports.content:
Noel Gallagher has never been prouder than about what sons did to angry Man United fans

Noel Gallagher says his heart swelled with pride as his son 'got stuck into' Manchester United fans at Sunday's derby.

Oasis star and die-hard Manchester City fan Gallagher was in the away end at Old Trafford as Erling Haaland's controversial goal won the game for the ten-man visitors.



3 Gallagher got to celebrate a Man City win on a rare trip to Old Trafford Credit: Getty

'My heart is full of pride'

And Gallagher revealed his son Sonny got thoroughly swept up in the occasion.

Speaking to Andy Goldstein and former Man United goalkeeper Ben Foster on talkSPORT DriveTime, he said: "There comes a point in your time as a father where you look at your children and you think, 'My god, I brought you up well' – when they feel it as much as you do and when they get it.

"Let's not forget, when you're in that away end and the United fans are in front of you, they're giving it to you as much as you're giving it to them.



"But he made the newspapers today and my heart is full of pride for my sons who got stuck into it yesterday and got stuck into the United fans as well."

A special day for the Gallagher family

Gallagher also revealed that it was his sons' – Sonny and brother Donovan – first trip to an away Manchester derby.



The pair were spotted jokingly taunting United fans by making crude gestures from the stands.

"Ordinarily I wouldn't [go]," Gallagher continued. "I don't like going to Old Trafford because it can get a bit spicy getting in and out, but they were there.



"They were so keen to go because they'd never been, so I went for them really and they got stuck into it big time and it was a great, great day."

Understandably, Gallagher was thrilled about the manner of City's victory.

Enzo Maresca's side played more than hour with ten men after Phil Foden's contentious red card for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes.

3 Haaland won the game with his sixth goal of the season Credit: Getty



3

"Obviously we celebrated like made for about five seconds [after Haaland's goal which was initially disallowed for offside]," Gallagher said. "We thought he looked offside even this morning.

"I was watching Match of the Day. He looks offside on the telly, so everyone thought it was offside, but it's the toenail of a boot.

"And no one's talking about the finish. How he got it in and across the other side of the goal is unbelievable.



"The fact that has gone our way [and] our whole strategy with 10 men is unbelievable."

Oasis to hit the road again in 2027

Gallagher also discussed Oasis' latest tour announcement, following their momentous 2025 reunion.

The Britpop icons will play 38 dates across Europe and North America next year.

They include a whopping 11 nights at City's Etihad Stadium and a return to Knebworth, the site of their legendary 1996 shows.

Sports.title: British sprint star Amy Hunt hits out at Sydney Sweeney for her naked betting advert which is 'sexualising women's sport' - as other athletes condemn actress for move and brand it 'a kick in the face'
Sports.content:
Sydney Sweeney has been accused of sexualising women’s sport by female Olympians after she posed naked in a betting advert.

The actress, 29, featured in a promotional video for bookmaker Novig in which she used various pieces of sports equipment to cover herself up.

The advert has drawn widespread condemnation from across the world of women’s sport, in particular from female Olympians.

British sprinter Amy Hunt – who became the first athlete to win four gold medals at a single European Championships earlier this year – used her post-race interview at the inaugural World Athletics Ultimate Championship to criticise the advert.

After finishing fourth in her 200m race, the 24-year-old said: 'It was incredible to be part of such an incredible race. Sydney Sweeney, this is what women is sport look like. 21.4 [seconds, the winning time of Melissa Jefferson-Wooden], muscles, hard work, sweat, blood, tears. This is a beautiful evening.'

The sprinter – who has previously called herself 'sexy and aggressive' – added that the reality of being a female athlete is rather different than Ms Sweeney's advert suggests.

Ms Hunt continued: 'Obviously we've seen in the last 24 hours everything about the Sydney Sweeney ad, you know, and when you're a woman in sport, it's not pretty. It's not glamorous. It's not sexy all the time, definitely.

'There's some low moments. Even turning up to this championship, my period started yesterday, so that's not really ideal, and that's not ever what you try to really plan for.'

Former Australian Olympic swimmer Ariarne Titmus, a four-time gold medallist, said: 'I can’t describe how infuriated I feel when I watch this.

'Not only is it a kick in the face to every woman who had dedicated her life to perfecting her craft, but every women who enjoys sports for what it really is – teamwork, friendship, dedication, excellent, unity.

'How do we live in a world where monetising a women’s body and sexualising women’s sport is still a thing?'

Sydney Sweeney has been accused of sexualising women’s sport by female Olympians after she posed naked in a betting advert

American gymnast Gracie Kramer also led the backlash against Ms Sweeney, posting a response on social media that read 'this is what a woman in sport looks like'.

It prompted a wave of responses from female athletes, including American diver Kassidy Cook, and has been liked more than a million times.

Fellow Australian Olympian Matilda Kearns shared a video montage featuring clips of the country's women's water polo team training and competing alongside the words: 'I absolutely f**king hate Sydney Sweeney's new sports ad.'

In the caption, she said: 'Like what are we doing… so much worse than I imagined too. Here's some real women's sports content.'

Australian world champion boxer Skye Nicolson said the advert made a 'mockery' of women in sport. She added on Instagram: 'There’s a big difference between looking "sexy" because you do sport compared to using sex to sell "sport".

'There is nothing wrong with looking good and doing sport and there’s nothing wrong with embracing your femininity while also being a badass athlete.'

British sprinter Hannah Williams also criticised the actress, posting a clip of runners with the caption: 'Hey Sydney Sweeney, this is women in sports.

'The ad is such a disgrace for woman in sports... constantly trying to be respected in a male dominated field.'

Ms Sweeney, 29, featured in a promotional video for bookmaker Novig in which she used various pieces of sports equipment to cover herself up

British sprinter Amy Hunt used her post-race interview at the inaugural World Athletics Ultimate Championship to criticise the actress

Olympic weightlifting coach Danielle Bagacay: 'The sexualisation of women in sport [and in life] is an ongoing issue that most [if not, all] women face.

'This issue disproportionately focuses on physical appearance and, instead, overshadows our achievements, hard work and ability to reach athletic goals.

'My purpose and mission as a coach is to focus on improving my athletes' ability, capacity and capability to reach their strength and performance goals.

'Less about the number on the scales or how they look, and more about feel and empowerment.

'I hope whatever Sydney Sweeney is trying to portray will be overshadowed by other women speaking/posting against the brand campaign.'

Fitness influencer Angela Everington wrote: 'Congratulations Sydney Sweeney, you've just rattled every woman in sport.

'45 per cent of teenage girls say they don't feel they have the 'right body shape' for sport.

'A study of women found 70 per cent had seen girls drop out of sport because of sports kit or body-image concerns.

'I'm sure your marketing would have performed just as well if you used your platform to share what the body can do rather than sexualise it.'

Olympian Matilda Kearns shared a video montage of the Australian national women's water polo team, which was captioned: 'I absolutely f**king hate Sydney Sweeney's new ad'

However, some have voiced support for Ms Sweeney, with one commenter writing on Ms Kearns' post: 'Easy to hate someone you are also jealous of.'

Another said: 'It still brought attention to women's sports... stop being such haters to another woman. Full stop. The end.'

'Why all the hate? What ever happened to women supporting women? She didn't kill her kids or anything,' someone else wrote.

The criticism comes after Novig founder and CEO Jacob Fortinsky revealed that Ms Sweeney, who holds an equity stake in the company, had pushed to appear nude in the campaign.

The Euphoria actress was reportedly drawn to the platform because it focuses strictly on sports predictions, while other platforms allow users to make predictions on a broader range of topics.

'She said, "I'm uncomfortable with other platforms that have markets on what colour underwear I'm going to wear",' Mr Fortinsky recalled in an interview with Front Office Sports.

He added: 'Sydney is great at captivating audiences and being the centre of attention.

Ms Sweeney defended herself by pointing out that male and female athletes have posed nude before

'In some sense, it forces us into the national discourse.'

Ms Sweeney has since hit back at critics of the advert, sharing a series of Instagram Stories that highlight female athletes who have appeared nude.

The actress posted photos of Serena Williams, Ronda Rousey, Sue Bird, Megan Rapinoe and Caroline Wozniacki posing for magazines.

She added that some male athletes have also previously posed nude.

It's not the first time an advertising campaign featuring Ms Sweeney has sparked fierce backlash.

Last year she starred in a controversial American Eagle jeans commercial which some deemed racist due to a pun linking 'jeans' and 'genes'.

The label's campaign featured the tagline: 'Sydney Sweeney Has Great Jeans.'

'Genes are passed down from parents to offspring, often determining traits like hair colour, personality and even eye colour... my genes are blue,' she said an accompanying video.

Last year the actress starred in a controversial American Eagle jeans advert which some deemed racist due to a pun linking 'jeans' and 'genes'

In the fallout, critics of the advert said it promoted eugenics, while US President Donald Trump showed his support for the actress and the brand.

Ms Sweeney told GQ that she found it 'surreal' that the scandal grew so big as to attract attention from the White House.

She said: 'I did a jean ad... I mean, the reaction definitely was a surprise, but I love jeans.

'All I wear are jeans. I'm literally in jeans and a T-shirt every day of my life.'

Critics accused the brand of echoing eugenicist language around 'good genes' and 'genetic superiority', claiming it appealed to Right-wing and white-nationalist groups online.

In August, American Eagle defended the campaign, insisting it 'always was about the jeans – her jeans, her story.'

Sports.title: Paul Scholes claims the 'jury is still out' on Senne Lammens - and insists Man United can't win the Premier League without a 'brilliant goalkeeper'
Sports.content:
Paul Scholes claims the 'jury is still out' on Senne Lammens - and insists Man United can't win the Premier League without a 'brilliant goalkeeper'

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Former Manchester United midfielder Paul Scholes has cast doubt on the ability of Red Devils goalkeeper Senne Lammens, despite his impressive start to life at Old Trafford.

The Belgian, who joined the club last summer for £21.7million from Royal Antwerp, has been United's undisputed No1 since displacing Altay Bayindir last autumn.

His performances have generally received praise from a fanbase who have not seen a settled goalkeeper since the days of David De Gea, but Scholes isn't sure.

'What team have you seen win the Premier League without a top class goalkeeper?' Scholes asked on his The Good, The Bad and The Football podcast. 'Lammens might be that, I don't know, I think the jury's probably still out on that and then you build from the back four.'

Lammens, 24, has previously made clear his plan to have a long career in Manchester, staking his claim to become a club legend.

He said last year: 'That's England for you. If things go badly, they can bury you deep, but if things go well, they praise you to the skies,' he added.

Paul Scholes has suggested 'the jury is still out' on Manchester United goalkeeper Senne Lammens (pictured)

Scholes (pictured) said United boss Michael Carrick may have to 'be patient and wait' for a top-class goalkeeper

'I take that with a grain of salt, because to be mentioned in the same sentence as Schmeichel, I'm going to have to prove myself many more times. But I did find it a very nice compliment.

'I hope to play here for 10 years and be important, so that, like Schmeichel and Van der Sar, I can leave a legacy.'

Scholes, though, isn't necessarily buying it. After Lammens was beaten by Erling Haaland's effort in the Manchester derby, the former midfielder said: 'It's the way Arsenal started three or four years ago, defensively they have been absolutely brilliant. You need a top class goalkeeper.

'You think of Liverpool's team with Alisson, Raya at Arsenal, Man United with Peter Schmeichel and Edwin van der Sar. They've all got brilliant, brilliant goalkeepers.

'You start from the back, of course you do. Whether Michael's (Carrick) just got to be patient and wait for that, I don't know.'

Sports.title: Former Premier League striker goes viral for calling out Howard Webb live on air and hitting out at 'unacceptable' decisions - as ex-ref Dermot Gallagher defends officials after Manchester derby blunder
Sports.content:
Jay Bothroyd has made waves on social media for calling out Pro Ref chief Howard Webb live on Sky Sports.

Webb and his referees have come under fire yet again following their Manchester derby slip up, which saw Erling Haaland's winning goal allowed to stand despite Enzo Fernandez clearly being offside in the build-up.

VAR officials Matt Donohue and Blake Antrobus have been stood down from duty for this weekend as a result of the fallout.

And Bothroyd, who played for the likes of Cardiff and Wolves in his career, has been one of the people leading the backlash as he let loose on Sky.

Bothroyd clashed with former top-level referee Dermot Gallagher, who had claimed referees 'know the law inside out'.

'Why did they get it wrong then?' the former forward asked.

Jay Bothroyd (right) has gone viral after calling out Howard Webb following the Manchester derby officiating blunder

When he was told the officials likely 'lost focus', a frustrated Bothroyd replied: 'This is the thing. To me, that is unacceptable. You can't lose focus. That is their job. Their only job is to look at this - they are under no pressure, they are in a room.

'There is more than one (VAR official). They need to be getting that right, it's as simple as that. And to be saying sorry afterwards, that's not good enough. Let's be real here - Michael Carrick is under pressure now. He could lose his job because of them making a bad decision and saying sorry. "Sorry, Michael, we've made a bad decision, but you've been sacked".'

Sky then showed a clip of Pro Ref chief Howard Webb saying a similar goal that United scored in the derby three years ago 'shouldn't happen again'.

Bothroyd continued: 'First of all, I need to say this, put the camera on me. Howard Webb, come on this show when it's live and speak to us, because you need to explain to us, so I can put you in the spotlight and ask you questions.

'You need to come and speak to me live on this show about this incident. Because I need to know this. We keep on hearing all these things, and I don't understand them.

'There are laws there, and they are not being followed. The understanding. The interpretation. Even yesterday (in the derby), they are saying sorry then trying to explain it and they are digging themselves a bigger hole.

'I don't understand it. I will put my money on it now and say it - this is the easiest decision I'm going to see all year and it's four games in.'

Despite Gallagher's protests, Bothroyd received widespread support for his words.

Erling Haaland's goal was allowed to stand despite Enzo Fernandez standing offside

Fernandez moved to head the ball, clearly impacting United's Lisandro Martinez and Senne Lammens

One fan wrote on X: 'Jay Bothroyd calling out Howard Webb on live TV was cinema. GOATed behaviour.'

Another posted: 'I watched this live. Jay Bothroyd has never backed down and always real. I love the way he quizzes referee Dermot Gallagher on Ref Watch. He's one of my favourites. Top player. Top analyst. Top man.'

A third shared: 'Standing ovation for Jay Bothroyd. Proper one.'

Webb regularly appears on pre-recorded TNT Sports show 'Match Officials: Mic'd Up', in which he analyses refereeing calls from games.

It was pointed out to Bothroyd that Webb has previously spoken live on incidents, but the forward called for him to go on Sky Sports too.

United defender Lisandro Martinez led the protests from United players after the game.

He said on Sky: 'It's the best league in the world, you have the best teams in the world, the best players in the world, and now we have to go home with this injustice.

'I think it was offside. What I can't understand is the rules. He (Fernandez) was there, in front of me, and I went to him. So that's why Haaland was free at the back.

'It's so hard because you lose a derby and you lose three points at home. Every season they're coming to our club and explaining the rules for an hour-and-a-half. They look so confident, and then after that five or six people are making these kind of mistakes. It's unacceptable.'

Sports.title: Leeds sniffed vulnerability and went for the kill in 4-1 horror show for Newcastle, writes CRAIG HOPE - this was a warning over where their season could end up, while Whites eye race for Europe
Sports.content:
Leeds sniffed vulnerability and went for the kill in 4-1 horror show for Newcastle, writes CRAIG HOPE - this was a warning over where their season could end up, while Whites eye race for Europe

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Identical records coming into this, poles and goals apart coming out. Leeds bullied and bettered Newcastle and are deservedly up to third in the Premier League.

Their unbeaten start is genuine and so are the prospects of them challenging for European football this season, nearly a quarter of a century after their last continental campaign.

Newcastle’s start always felt less real, and so it proved on a night when Daniel Farke’s side were as brilliant and boisterous as those in the stands. Elland Road was a bear pit and, from the off, it was clear that their visitors were in for a mauling. To think, they’re in the process of making this place even bigger and more intimidating.

Those words capture Dominic Calvert-Lewin, too. He should be in Thomas Tuchel’s England squad this week after a centre-forward showing that was as powerful as it was precise. He deserved two goals - the dubious awards panel gave his first to a strand of Jayden Bogle’s hair - but there is no such committee to rob him of the man-of-the-match prize.

‘It was a top-class performance during the whole game,’ said Farke. ‘But we can’t get cocky or too big-time. This should give us huge confidence going forward.

‘As for Dominic, he is one of the best strikers in the league in this form.’

This 3-0 Leeds defeat marked the night the result caught up with their performances

Dominic Calvert-Lewin was the star of the show as he continued his fine form at Elland Road

For Newcastle, this was a night when the result finally caught up with performance. Unbeaten in three at the outset of the Premier League and lauded for their summer business, autumn and winter might not be so cheery on the evidence of this horror show.

Matthias Jaissle’s side were three down by half-time, and it was no surprise at all. Be that on the basis of what played out here or, more so, performances of the past 10 days. An unconvincing 1-0 win at Millwall in the Carabao Cup came on the back of an equally sketchy 2-2 draw at home to Bournemouth.

This, then, was in the post, and Calvert-Lewin was the home side’s delivery man. He was not the only one to profit from opposition weak in the tackle, wayward in the pass and woefully short of ideas in attack. Leeds captain Ethan Ampadu bossed a midfield that was superior by every metric.

At times, you wondered if the hosts had an extra man. You wondered more how Newcastle have won such praise for their character and resilience in recent weeks. There were none of those traits on show this time.

Jaissle said: ‘Not only one thing went wrong. We couldn’t bring the fundamentals in the first half. We couldn’t match the intensity of Leeds, in duals or physicality. That should be the basics of football. Unforced errors were taking place. We needed to find the right reaction on the pitch, and we struggled with that.’

Newcastle’s numbers have not felt sustainable. They had conceded a league-high 45 shots over the first three games and, at the other end, their cumulative XG was just over one per 90 minutes.

This will infuriate traditionalists - those who cherish the scoreline - but an expected league position had Newcastle 19th going into this weekend.

A lot, it seemed, rested on the slender shoulders on Matias Fernandez-Pardo in reversing the numbers. The 21-year-old, a £51million marquee arrival from Lille this month, was making his full debut. ‘Eden Hazard without the end product’ was how one Belgian journalist described the forward on the day he signed, much to the irritation of black-and-white ears listening on local radio. So, was there any merit in the unflattering assessment?

MATCH FACTS AND PLAYER RATINGS Leeds (3-4-2-1): Trafford 6; Justin 7, Elvedi 6, Muharemovic 6; Bogle 7, Ampadu 8, Tanaka 8 (Aaronson 72, 6), Gudmundsson 7 (Bard 72, 6); Stach 6, Okafor 7 (Wilson 72, 6); Calvert-Lewin 9 Subs: Zetterer, Bard, Bijol, Longstaff, Aaronson, Wilson, James, Bahoya, Nmecha Manager: Daniel Farke 8 Newcastle (4-2-3-1): Hornicek 5; Dedic 5 (Livramento 57), Thiaw 5, Botman 3, Hall 5; Miley 4 (Bamba 80), Gonzalez 5 (Steur 19, 4); Murphy 4 (Toure 57, 6), Wissa 5, Barnes 4; Fernandez-Pardo 4 (Willock 57, 4) Subs: Pope, Livramento, Schar, Bamba, Toure, Willock, Ramsey, M Miley Manager: Matthias Jaissle 4 Ref: M Salisbury 7

After 25 minutes, the hot-takes felt cold, given Fernandez-Pardo had touched the ball only four times, and one of those was an accidental handball inside his own area. By the time he made way in the 57th minute, the touch count had reached 15, but none of them memorable. What Fernandez-Pardo learnt here is that speed of foot counts for nothing when faced with speed of thought.

‘We had to bury the game after a good start and that is what we did,’ said Farke.

Leeds’ third goal on the stroke of half-time was the one that sealed the zip on Newcastle’s body bag. That goal was about Calvert-Lewin’s force and Newcastle’s complete lack of it, the striker barging his way through Sven Botman before finishing from six yards.

The opener, 13 minutes earlier, was officially a Lewis Miley own goal, but it owed everything to Ao Tanaka, who started the move amid space in midfield and finished it amid space in midfield. It was his 20-yard shot that deflected in off the Newcastle youngster, who like many of his team-mates endured a torrid night. His midfield sidekick, Sean Steur, was guilty of the stray pass that set Leeds on their way to a second, when Calvert-Lewin headed in from a James Justin cross, only for replays to reveal the ball clipping the head of Bogle.

Marquee signing Matias Fernandez-Pardo struggled, but that says more about the failings behind him

Technical weaknesses were always likely to catch up with the Magpies this season

The fourth, in the 59th minute, was a smart Noah Okafor finish after he reacted quickest to a loose ball from a long throw-in. But Leeds had been quicker to first, second and third balls all night.

The home fans were chanting for five when Baz Toure nicked an 89th-minute consolation. The away end had long since lost their voice and their solemn mood reflected a team who had made precious little noise on the pitch. This was a brutal reality check and serves as a warning for where their season could be headed.

Leeds, meanwhile, are looking up - at Arsenal and Manchester City.

Sports.title: Tom Aspinall announces he is vacating UFC heavyweight title after 'multiple surgeries, accidents and infections' as British fighter admits he's 'absolutely gutted' in emotional social media post
Sports.content:
Tom Aspinall announces he is vacating UFC heavyweight title after 'multiple surgeries, accidents and infections' as British fighter admits he's 'absolutely gutted' in emotional social media post

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Tom Aspinall has vacated his UFC heavyweight title due to 'ongoing complications' with eye injuries.

The Englishman last fought in October last year, when his title defence against Ciryl Gane ended as a no-contest after multiple eye pokes.

Aspinall was subsequently diagnosed with a rare condition called Brown's syndrome in both eyes and has had multiple surgeries, but he is still not ready to compete.

He wrote on Instagram: 'I’m absolutely gutted. I’ve chased this dream since I was 10 years old.

'I’m not done. Stepping away from the title is not stepping away from the sport or the dream. I’ll continue doing everything I can to get healthy, get cleared and get back to competing as soon as possible.

'What makes this particularly difficult is that many of the complications I’m dealing with are a result of fouls that changed the course of my career. Fighters rely on officials to enforce the rules and protect us in those moments, and it’s hard to still be dealing with the consequences today.'

Tom Aspinall has vacated his UFC heavyweight title due to 'ongoing complications' with eyes injuries

He was diagnosed with a rare condition Brown's syndrome following an eye poke at UFC 321

He also said: 'Ongoing complications with my eyes mean I cannot get medically cleared to fight right now.

'I’ve had multiple surgeries, accidents and infections, and done everything possible to get back to competing.

'I had previously agreed to a fight date and was back sparring, feeling great and ready to compete when an accident caused further damage to my right eye. This means more time away from the sport, and right now, the timing of my return is unclear.'

He added: 'I’ve now made the decision to vacate the heavyweight title. I’ve asked the UFC to allow me to make this statement because I don’t want to hold the heavyweight division up. I know what it’s like to have your career put on hold and I want the other fighters to have the opportunity to compete for the title.'

Aspinall returned to training in June with a view to fighting Gane in September but the wait will have to go on.

In August, Aspinall rebuffed suggestions that he would leave the UFC.

Against Gane in October, Aspinall retained his UFC heavyweight title via no contest in an anticlimactic ending to the main event at UFC 321 that saw the Brit struggling to see and rushed to hospital.

He does intend to return to fighting in the UFC but is unable to at the moment

After four minutes of the first round of the fight in Abu Dhabi, as Aspinall attempted a kick, Gane went at his rival with a punch and inadvertently raked his fingers across his eyes. A five-minute timeout ensued, and the doctor stepped in.

Aspinall was spotted telling the doctor: 'I can't see,' with the doctor himself telling the referee that he had 'no immediate concerns about the globe'.

After four minutes of the five allocated, however, the fight was waved off as a no-contest.

'All that training for that,' Aspinall said. 'What the f*** is he doing?

'He got warned twice before it. Twice before it he got warned for it and he f***ing did it again.'

Gane, however, said: 'I didn't do it on purpose. I know what it's like to have an eye poke, because when I fought Derrick Lewis, I got an eye poke and I was seeing two of Derrick Lewis for a full round.

'During a bit of the round and the rest of the round, I saw two of Derrick Lewis. So I'm not going to say, he's a liar.'

Aspinall, who was sat with his eye strapped up, added: 'I could feel how deep it was in my eye. It feels like the back of my eyeball is hurting. It feels like someone's touched the back of my eyeball.

Sports.title: Hilarious moment 'raging' Dominic Calvert-Lewin is told by referee his goal was taken off him after team-mate's tiny deflection
Sports.content:
Leeds forward Dominic Calvert-Lewin gave a hilarious reaction to being told his side's second goal had been taken away from him on Monday night. The Whites thumped Newcastle 4-1 in a stellar performance at Elland Road, with four different players, ultimately, on the scoresheet for the home side. Calvert-Lewin scored the third goal, but thought he had also netted the second when he headed in from James Justin's cross. But replays showed his header came off team-mate Jayden Bogle, and the full back was officially credited with the goal. Sky cameras managed to capture the exact moment Calvert-Lewin was told the goal wasn't actually his, with his face dropping in disbelief when he was told by an official at half-time. 'The ref told me at half-time they gave it to Jayden,' he said on Sky Sports after the match. 'I didn't even know he was there as I got up early and bang. I'll take the assist.' This is the hilarious moment Dominic Calvert-Lewin (right) found out Leeds' second goal against Newcastle had actually been awarded to Jayden Bogle (left) Calvert-Lewin joked after the game that he would be looking to appeal the decision Bogle, meanwhile, said: 'I didn't know anything about it. I said to the ref I didn't fancy telling him at half-time. Even during the game he was still a bit raging. He's happy with the points though.' And the saga carried on after the game. Calvert-Lewin and Bogle posed for a snap together, with the forward writing: 'He's told me that it didn't touch him. How do I appeal this scandalous decision?' He also tagged the Premier League. Calvert-Lewin would later finish well from Tarik Muharemovic's pass, making it 3-0 to his side. Lewis Miley's own goal opened the scoring and Noah Okafor's finish made it 4-0 before Bazoumana Traore netted a late consolation. The result moved Leeds up to third in the Premier League, with Newcastle sat in 12th.

Sports.title: West Ham legend Ludek Miklosko dead aged 64: Tributes pour in for 'gentle giant' as former Hammers goalkeeper and coach passes away after long battle with cancer
Sports.content:
West Ham legend Ludek Miklosko dead aged 64: Tributes pour in for 'gentle giant' as former Hammers goalkeeper and coach passes away after long battle with cancer

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

West Ham paid tribute to their cult hero and 'gentle giant' Ludek Miklosko who has died at the age of 64.

Miklosko kept 126 clean sheets in eight years with the Hammers and is perhaps best remembered for an inspirational series of saves to deny Manchester United the title in 1995.

The popular Czech, signed from Banik Ostrava for £300,000, later returned to the club as goalkeeper coach and fans have continued to sing his name for many years.

West Ham's players held a moment of silence before training on Monday, and the club will honour him before Wednesday's Carabao Cup third round tie against Fulham.

There are also plans for a tribute at next month's Championship fixture against Queens Park Rangers, where Miklosko spent the final three years of his playing career.

'Rest in peace Ludek, our beloved, inspirational goalkeeper and gentle giant of a man,' said West Ham in a statement released on Monday.

Legendary former West Ham goalkeeper Ludek Miklosko has died aged 64 after a cancer battle

The much-loved Czech 'gentle giant' made 373 outings for West Ham and also played for QPR

'Ludo', left, was a hugely popular figure at West Ham and tributes have been pouring in for him

Miklosko, who won 42 international caps and represent Czechoslovakia at the World Cup in 1990, was diagnosed with cancer in 2021 and announced three years later his decision to withdraw from further treatment.

His son Martin said: 'We are heartbroken to announce the passing of my Dad Ludek, following a brave and courageous battle with cancer.

'On behalf of my Mum and my family, I would like to sincerely thank the fans and everyone at West Ham United Football Club for the kind wishes, thoughts and prayers that were sent to my Dad during his illness.

'We know that the many messages and wishes from his former team-mates and fans alike were a huge sense of comfort to him in his battle with cancer and gave him the strength to not give up and keep fighting for as long as he could.

'We are heartbroken at his loss but take huge comfort from the immense support he received from all of you, along with the knowledge that he is now at peace and no longer suffering.

'Dad simply loved West Ham United, and especially hearing his name sung loud and proud at every game. The club, and its fans, were and always will be a part of our family, so thank you all from the bottom of our hearts.'

Sports.title: Richarlison aims social media dig at Roberto De Zerbi after unhappy star was exiled by Tottenham boss - and won't even play in Carabao Cup at Liverpool
Sports.content:
Richarlison aims social media dig at Roberto De Zerbi after unhappy star was exiled by Tottenham boss - and won't even play in Carabao Cup at Liverpool

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Tottenham forward Richarlison has taken aim at his manager Roberto De Zerbi after the Spurs boss rejected the chance to call him up for his side's Carabao Cup game at Liverpool.

The forward has been left out of his club's Premier League squad, but is available for selection in the League Cup.

Spurs have failed to score in their first four Premier League games this season, an embarrassment heightened by the omission of Richarlison – last season's top scorer with 12 goals – from the squad.

'Nothing changes in my project, in my idea,' said De Zerbi. 'I am sorry for the goals we didn't score, but we have the qualities to score goals.

'We are building a new project, a new team. I can't change my opinion about the players if they don't win or don't score. They are very good players.

'If we want to change from the last two seasons, we have to be stronger and believe in the quality of the players and the decisions we made one month ago. You can change players or change coaches, change, change, change, and nothing changes. Or you stay humble, with the right spirit to work.

Richarlison has taken aim at Roberto De Zerbi after his manager revealed he will not play the Brazilian in the League Cup

'I believe in my players. I hope they believe in themselves like I believe in them.'

But Richarlison has snapped back. Taking to Instagram, he replied to an X post around De Zerbi's comments with a crying emoji, and then shared a screenshot of the post to Instagram with the caption: 'Why' with another crying emoji.

Richarlison started the league opener at Brentford, but was told he can leave before a move to Everton collapsed and links to Trabzonspor failed to turn into a move.

After he did not agree personal terms with boyhood club Vasco on Friday, he was in attendance for Spurs' goalless draw with Everton, but will remain on the sidelines.

De Zerbi, who will be without Sandro Tonali against Liverpool after the midfielder picked up a knock, took his players out to dinner last week as he did in April, after they lost at Sunderland in his first game in charge. They returned to Mediterranean restaurant Bacchanalia in Mayfair and the Spurs boss picked up the bill.

'Something to eat, some water, some beers,' said De Zerbi. 'It is a pleasure.'

De Zerbi pored over the first half-hour of Saturday's 0-0 draw with Everton to analyse why his side could not convert their dominance into goals.

'We played 25-30 minutes very well,' said De Zerbi. 'We could have scored two. We maybe lost confidence because we didn't score. We have to improve.'

Richarlison, having demanded to leave Spurs in the summer and then failed to agree personal terms with Everton, Trabzonspor or Vasco da Gama, will remain out in the cold.

'We lost at Brentford 3-0 [on the opening day] with Richarlison,' De Zerbi added. 'Maybe you forgot. Just to remind you.'

Sports.title: Arsenal call up summer signing from Man Utd as Mikel Arteta prepares changes
Sports.content:
Arsenal call up summer signing from Man Utd as Mikel Arteta prepares changes

Arsenal have called up a host of young stars, including James Scanlon, who joined the club from Manchester United recently, as they prepare for their Carabao Cup clash with Ipswich

View 2 Images Arsenal could hand opportunities to some of their young talents at Ipswich, with James Scanlon among those in contention

Mikel Arteta has called up Arsenal youngster James Scanlon, who signed this summer from Manchester United, ahead of their clash with Ipswich.

‌



The fixtures continue to come thick and fast for the Gunners as they prepare to begin their Carabao Cup efforts. It is their fourth game in nine days, with the last three of those all coming on the road, and changes are expected.

‌



Scanlon could be one of the major beneficiaries with wingers Bukayo Saka and Christos Tzolis potentially being given a break. Noni Madueke and Eberechi Eze are their likely replacements but it could leave spots on the bench for the likes of Scanlon and Max Dowman, who is highly thought of in north London.

‌



Scanlon was seen in Monday’s training session at the club’s London Colney base ahead of Tuesday night’s cup tie at Portman Road, reports the Evening Standard.

‌



A host of young talents made the step up to first-team training, which was likely preparation for some of them being involved at Ipswich. Marli Salmon, Jaden Dixon and Andre Harriman-Annous were all part of the main group.

Scanlond, 19, has already played 24 times on the international scene having been capped by Gibraltar and last year had a loan stint away at Swindon. He's yet to play for Arsenal but has talked up what he could bring.

“I like to score goals, assist, so hopefully I can excite players who watch me,” he said in the summer. “I’m looking forward to playing, representing the badge, improving and hopefully showing people what I can do.”

‌



View 2 Images James Scanlon swapped Manchester for Arsenal in the summer (Image: Getty Images)

Arteta has previously used the early rounds of the Carabao Cup to hand opportunities to younger players, last season Harriman-Annous made his first outing during a game against Brighton.

Arsenal have endured notable frustration in the Carabao Cup over recent years and it remains a trophy that has eluded Arteta. It was also never captured by Arsene Wenger in his 20-plus years at the club meaning Arsenal haven't won it since 1993. Last year they were losing finalists to Manchester City and the year prior they were undone in the semi-finals by eventual winners Newcastle.

Sports.title: Howard Webb under growing pressure after Man Utd apology and Arsenal complaint
Sports.content:
Howard Webb under growing pressure after Man Utd apology and Arsenal complaint

Several Premier League clubs have major concerns over refereeing mistakes after another weekend of controversial decisions, most notably in the Manchester derby

View 3 Images Pro Ref chief Howard Webb is under pressure

Referees' chief Howard Webb is under mounting pressure after another huge blunder from his officials.

‌



Webb, Pro Ref’s chief refereeing officer, has axed the VAR team Matt Donohue and Blake Antrobus from next weekend’s Premier League fixtures after allowing Erling Haaland's winner to stand in the Manchester derby.

‌



Pro Ref have already been forced to contact Manchester United to explain the “error of judgment” as they failed to disallow City striker Haaland’s goal despite Enzo Fernandez being in an offside position and interfering with play.

‌



Arsenal have also made contact with Webb following Mikel Arteta ’s post-match rant that a penalty was given against Ezri Konsa for a challenge on Sunderland's Dan Ballard.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



It is understood Arsenal want an explanation about why the decision was given by referee John Brooks.

Referees are under orders to clamp down on penalty box grappling but Arsenal may feel they have been unfairly targeted because similar incidents went unpunished in other games.

It has left Webb feeling the heat and Mirror Sport understands that several clubs have major concerns about consistency, new directives - like grappling this season - not being applied fairly and why huge mistakes continue to happen.

‌



Webb has been in there job for coming up to four years and, while there is an acceptance that he is determined to drive change and they like his communication, there is frustration about refereeing standards.

View 3 Images Arsenal were furious after conceding a penalty during their win over Sunderland

United defender Lisandro Martinez described Haaland’s goal as an “injustice” because he and teammate, keeper Senne Lammens, were influenced by Fernandez’s presence.

‌



It has caused disbelief in football circles and the Haaland howler was compared to former Liverpool striker Luis Diaz’s goal being wrongly disallowed at Tottenham in 2023 which is widely regarded as the biggest blunder in VAR history.

Donohue and Antrobus have been stood down but Webb has got some explaining to do to clubs in the next Premier League shareholders’ meeting and also the next edition of Match Officials Mic’D Up.

View 3 Images Michael Oliver appears to have been absolved of blame (Image: Getty Images)

‌



But referee Michael Oliver, who was in charge at Old Trafford, is down to officiate Sunday’s match between Bournemouth and Liverpool so it would appear that he has been absolved of blame.

Former Premier League referee Dermot Gallagher says the officials “lost focus” and that is why they did not give an offside rather than a goal. Gallagher told Sky: “I think they are so focused on whether Fernandez touches the ball - he doesn’t - that they’ve lost focus.

“He’s clearly gone to head the ball. If you watch, Lammens is the first affected because he goes to make the save, Martinez is dragged away from Haaland because he’s got to go to it.”

Sports.title: OLI BELL: "We should be telling the world about horse racing's success stories"
Sports.content:
Saturdays history making win from Saffie Osborne in the Betfred St Leger was as good a day on the racecourse as I can remember.

About 30,000 racegoers, revelling in the sunshine, fully aware of the magnitude of what they had just witnessed.

Doncaster and the team at Arena Racing deserve huge credit for the work they put in to make the 250th St Leger a fitting day for the occasion. They were rewarded for their efforts with the fairytale result.

It’s vital that the sport shouts loudly about days like Saturday. All too often recently we have been talking negatively about the future of the sport, and whilst clearly there are challenges ahead, if we keep repeating a negative message then surely that is the message that will seep out into the wider world.

‌



The sport of horse racing on its day, as Saturday highlighted so perfectly, is unmatched. Therefore, repeating, quite loudly that racing has its detractors, or that there are dark clouds on the horizon is a very damaging narrative to put into the public psyche.

This isn’t me saying we should bury our heads in the sand if there is a bad news story but there are plenty of things out of most people’s control.

Of the 30,000-plus at Doncaster on Saturday I reckon 99.99% of them couldn’t give two hoots if Arc, the Jockey Club, Ascot and the RCA were at loggerheads.

View 2 Images ITV presenter Oli Bell says racing should be shouting loudly about the sport's success stories (Image: ITV)

‌



Thankfully Martin Cruddace told me on ITV's The Opening Show that there are positive conversations being had behind the scenes in that space.

But that’s exactly it isn’t it…. There are very smart people in racing, in high powered roles that we need to trust to do their jobs well and for the best interest of the long term health of the sport.

Rather than publicly peddling a narrative of infighting and issues, we need to spend our energies telling the world that racing, no matter anything going on behind the scenes. is truly magical.

Saturday showed us that. Racing always shows us that.

‌



The point is... whenever something good happens we don’t need to air our dirty laundry. We need to be yelling about the fact that racing, a sport that allows men and women to compete equally, has just witnessed a groundbreaking, historic, inspirational moment.

We need to be ensuring every news station is aware of it. We need to be campaigning to get Saffie short listed for BBC SPOTY. We need to be making sure that everyone, whether they like racing or not is aware of these moments of unbridled joy that only the sport of racing can serve up.

In Saffie and soon-to-be-champion jockey Billy Loughnane the sport of racing has two generational stars that can cross into the mainstream and bring new fans into the sport.

Let’s spend more time telling the world about them and their achievements rather then who is bickering with who.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
